sentences.en: All over the field, Roman soldiers lay dead in their thousands, horse and foot mingled, as the shifting phases of the battle, or the attempt to escape, had brought them together.
sentences.zh: 战场各处，数以千计的罗马士兵横尸遍野，骑兵与步兵混杂在一起，如同随着战局的变幻或逃生的企图而聚拢到了一起。

sentences.en: Here and there, wounded men, covered with blood, who had been roused to consciousness by the morning cold,
sentences.zh: 偶有浑身是血的伤员，被清晨的寒意唤醒了知觉，

sentences.en: were dispatched by a quick blow as they struggled to rise from amongst the corpses.
sentences.zh: 在他们挣扎着从尸堆中爬起时，被速战速决地一击毙命。

sentences.en: Others were found still alive, with the sinews in their thighs and behind their knees sliced through.
sentences.zh: 另有一些人被发现时犹有气息，大腿和膝盖后侧的肌腱已被割断。

sentences.en: Bearing their throats and necks, and begging who would, to spill what little blood they had left.
sentences.zh: 他们裸露出喉咙和颈部，恳求过往之人放干他们体内仅存的一点血。

sentences.en: Some had their heads buried in the ground, having apparently dug themselves holes, and by smothering their faces with earth, had choked themselves to death.
sentences.zh: 有些人将头埋进土里，显然是自己挖了洞，将脸埋在泥土中，活活把自己窒息而死。

sentences.en: Most strange of all was a Numidian soldier, still living and lying, with nose and ears horribly lacerated,
sentences.zh: 最离奇的莫过于一名努米底亚士兵，他尚有呼吸，倒在一名罗马人的尸体下方，鼻子和耳朵被撕裂得面目全非，

sentences.en: underneath the body of a Roman, who when his useless hands had no longer been able to grasp his sword, had died in the act of tearing his enemy in bestial fury with his teeth.
sentences.zh: 当他无力的双手再也无法握住宝剑时，至死都在用牙齿带着野兽般的狂怒撕咬着敌人。

sentences.en: So that was the account of the battlefield of Cannae by Livy, and he's describing the morning after, one of the bloodiest and most notorious days in the entire history,
sentences.zh: 以上就是李维对坎尼战场的记述，他所描述的是战后次日清晨的景象，这是整个历史上最血腥、最臭名昭著的日子之一，

sentences.en: not just of Rome or of the Punic Wars, but of armed conflict generally, because this is one of the most studied, most discussed, most famous battles in all world history.
sentences.zh: 不仅对罗马或布匿战争而言，对整个武装冲突史而言都是如此，因为这是世界历史上研究最多、讨论最多、最著名的战役之一。

sentences.en: It took place on the 2nd of August, 216 BC.
sentences.zh: 它发生于公元前216年8月2日。

sentences.en: And Tom, for the Romans, this was the darkest day in all their history, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，对于罗马人来说，这是他们历史上最黑暗的一天，对吧？

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And for as long as their empire endured,
sentences.zh: 并且在他们的帝国存续期间，

sentences.en: Roman historians who wanted to emphasize some particular shattering defeat would say, oh, this was the worst day ever, except for Cannae.
sentences.zh: 想要强调某种毁灭性惨败的罗马历史学家会说，哦，这是有史以来最糟糕的一天，除了坎尼之战。

sentences.en: And they would always acknowledge that even the worst defeat wasn't as terrible as Cannae had been.
sentences.zh: 他们总是会承认，即使是最惨重的失败也没有坎尼之战那么可怕。

sentences.en: And I think what is fascinating is that modern historians as well have been kind of equally fascinated
sentences.zh: 而且我认为迷人之处在于，现代历史学家同样也深深着迷于

sentences.en: by the scale of the slaughter that was inflicted on Rome on that terrible day.
sentences.zh: 在那个可怕的日子里罗马所遭受的屠杀规模。

sentences.en: So there are two really excellent studies of this battle.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于这场战役有两部非常优秀的研究著作。

sentences.en: One by Greg Daly at Cannae, the experience of battle in the 2nd Punic War.
sentences.zh: 一部是格雷戈·戴利的《坎尼：第二次布匿战争中的战斗体验》。

sentences.en: He writes,
sentences.zh: 他写道：

sentences.en: Very striking fact that there were more Romans and Italians killed in one day of fighting at Cannae than Americans killed in combat during the whole Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 一个非常惊人的事实是，在坎尼一日的战斗中阵亡的罗马人和意大利人，比整个越南战争期间在战斗中阵亡的美国人还要多。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good fact.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的事实。

sentences.en: I mean, that's an amazing stat.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一个惊人的统计数据。

sentences.en: And then Adrian Goldsworthy, who is essentially what my brother is to the 2nd World War.
sentences.zh: 然后是阿德里安·戈兹沃西，他之于罗马军队，

sentences.en: He is to the Roman army.
sentences.zh: 就像我兄弟之于第二次世界大战一样。

sentences.en: I mean, he is the goat on this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他就是这个领域的历史第一人。

sentences.en: And he wrote an excellent book on Cannae as well.
sentences.zh: 他也写过一本关于坎尼的出色著作。

sentences.en: And it has an introduction from Richard Holmes, you know, the great military historian.
sentences.zh: 书中包含了理查德·霍姆斯——你知道的，那位伟大的军事历史学家——所作的序言。

sentences.en: And Richard Holmes writes,
sentences.zh: 理查德·霍姆斯写道：

sentences.en: The Romans lost more men killed than the British army on the first day of the Somme in 1916.
sentences.zh: 罗马人阵亡的人数超过了1916年索姆河战役第一天的英国军队。

sentences.en: Which I guess for British people is always the kind of, it's the measuring stick of pointless slaughter, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这对于英国人来说一直是无意义屠杀的衡量标准，对吧？

sentences.en: But of course, those are Vietnam and the First World War, both industrialized conflicts.
sentences.zh: 但当然，越南战争和第一次世界大战都是工业化冲突。

sentences.en: So the idea that a battle in the ancient world could have a scale of slaughter to rank alongside the conflicts of the modern age just seems extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 因此，古代世界的一场战役其屠杀规模竟能与现代冲突相提并论，这似乎非同寻常。

sentences.en: But it's not the only reason why Cannae is such a famous battle, is it?
sentences.zh: 但坎尼之战如此闻名，可不仅仅只有这一个原因，对吧？

sentences.en: It's also famous because, you know, for people who are great students of military tactics, this is like sort of Maradona's second goal against England in 1986,
sentences.zh: 它之所以出名，还因为对于军事战术的狂热研究者来说，这就好比马拉多纳在1986年对阵英格兰时的第二个进球一样，

sentences.en: or one of Lionel Messi's great performances of Roger Federer or something.
sentences.zh: 或者像利昂内尔·梅西的巅峰表现、罗杰·费德勒的比赛之类的。

sentences.en: It is the acme of perfection.
sentences.zh: 这是完美的极致。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: It is the absolute archetype of a vastly outnumbered force annihilating a much superior one.
sentences.zh: 它是绝对的典范，展现了绝对劣势的兵力彻底消灭一支远优于己的军队。

sentences.en: And it's for that reason, I think, as Greg Daly puts it in his book, that Cannae may be the most studied battle in history.
sentences.zh: 正是因为这个原因，我认为，正如格雷格·戴利在他的书中所说，坎尼之战可能是历史上被研究最多的战役。

sentences.en: Because obviously, if you can distill the elixir, if you can work out the formula that Hannibal applied,
sentences.zh: 因为显然，如果你能提炼出这种灵药，如果你能找出汉尼拔所运用的公式，

sentences.en: then hopefully you can apply that to your own age and win similarly stunning victories.
sentences.zh: 那么你就有希望把它应用到你自己的时代，并赢得同样惊艳的胜利。

sentences.en: And I mean, you'll know this, Dominic, as a student historian of the First World War, that First World War generals and strategists were obsessed by Cannae.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，多米尼克，作为一名研究第一次世界大战的学生历史学家，你会知道这一点，一战的将领和战略家们对坎尼之战简直着迷。

sentences.en: So Schlieffen is the kind of the famous example that he was the chief of the German general staff,
sentences.zh: 所以施利芬就是一个著名的例子，他是德国总参谋长，

sentences.en: wasn't he, in kind of before the First World War, devised this, the Schlieffen plan, or did he?
sentences.zh: 对吧，在一战前夕，制定了这个施利芬计划，或者说真的是他吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I know it's very controversial.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道这很有争议。

sentences.en: But essentially, the German high command were aiming at a battle of annihilation that was consciously inspired by what Hannibal had done.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，德国最高指挥部旨在发动一场有意识地受到汉尼拔所作所为启发的歼灭战。

sentences.en: And after the war, there was a collection of his essays published that just had the title Cannae.
sentences.zh: 战后，曾出版过一本他的论文集，书名就叫《坎尼》。

sentences.en: And then in the Second World War, on the Eastern Front, again, lots of Hitler's generals were obsessed with replicating Hannibal's tactics.
sentences.zh: 然后到了第二次世界大战的东线战场，希特勒的许多将领同样痴迷于复制汉尼拔的战术。

sentences.en: So Guderian, in particular, with his tanks, warring across the Eastern Front.
sentences.zh: 所以古德里安尤其如此，他带着坦克在东线纵横驰骋。

sentences.en: He was very inspired by the example of the Carthaginian cavalry at Cannae.
sentences.zh: 他深受坎尼之战中迦太基骑兵样板的启发。

sentences.en: And weirdly, Americans with German names were also obsessed.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，有着德国姓氏的美国人也对此着迷。

sentences.en: So Eisenhower was obsessed by it, and more recently, Norman Schwarzkopf, who commanded the American forces in Desert Storm.
sentences.zh: 所以艾森豪威尔对此着迷，更近一点的还有诺曼·施瓦茨科普夫，他指挥了沙漠风暴行动中的美军。

sentences.en: He was always going on about how his tactics and strategy there were modelled on Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 他总是喋喋不休地说他在那里的战术和战略是以汉尼拔为蓝本的。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing that I imagine that if I was to study at West Point, a man in a bow tie would talk about this battle for weeks.
sentences.zh: 我想象如果我去西点军校学习，这大概会是那种系着领结的人连续几个星期都在谈论的战役。

sentences.en: Firstly, talk about Thucydides.
sentences.zh: 首先，谈谈修昔底德。

sentences.en: And then they'd have you as a guest lecturer or something, Tom.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会请你作为客座讲师之类的，汤姆。

sentences.en: It'd be awful.
sentences.zh: 那会很糟糕。

sentences.en: It'd be soul-destroying.
sentences.zh: 那会让人灵魂崩溃。

sentences.en: Oh, what, for the listeners or for me?
sentences.zh: 哦，什么，对听众还是对我？

sentences.en: No, I mean, you'd be handsomely remunerated.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，你会得到丰厚的报酬。

sentences.en: But I, as a student, I'd first have to endure the lecture by the man in the bow tie, and then you pitching up to give an hour-long lecture, and my life would be in ruins.
sentences.zh: 但我作为一个学生，首先得忍受那个系领结的人的讲座，然后你又跳出来进行长达一小时的演讲，我的生活就全毁了。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's move on.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们继续吧。

sentences.en: This is an amazing subject, because the thing is that there is a risk with viewing Cannae as a kind of platonic ideal of a battle.
sentences.zh: 这是一个了不起的主题，因为问题在于，把坎尼视为一场战役的柏拉图式理想形态是有风险的。

sentences.en: Because if you abstract it, you get away from what actually makes the study of this battle,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你把它抽象化，你就偏离了让这场战役的研究真正具有吸引力、令人不安甚至极其恐怖的东西，

sentences.en: of maybe all the battles in ancient history, so compelling and so unsettling and actually terrifying.
sentences.zh: 也许古代历史上的所有战役都是如此。

sentences.en: Because what both Daly and Goldsworthy do in their two actually quite different books, but in one thing they're very similar.
sentences.zh: 因为戴利和戈德斯沃西在他们两本其实截然不同的书中，有一个共同点非常相似。

sentences.en: They really emphasize the physicality of warfare generally, but specifically in this battle.
sentences.zh: 他们真正强调了战争普遍的物质性，尤其是这场战役中的物质性。

sentences.en: And it reminds us that Cannae is a battle that is fought in the context of the much broader war that we've been talking about in this series, between distinctive commanders,
sentences.zh: 这提醒我们，坎尼之战是在我们本系列一直在讨论的更广泛的战争背景下进行的，这场战争发生在杰出的统帅之间、

sentences.en: between distinctive armies, cities, ways of life.
sentences.zh: 杰出的军队、城市和生活方式之间。

sentences.en: And the ancient sources, and you quoted Livy, but we have Polybius as well, we have Plutarch,
sentences.zh: 古代的资料源头——你引用了李维，但我们也有波利比乌斯，我们还有普鲁塔克——

sentences.en: they are unusually visceral in their accounts of what actually happens when the Roman and the Carthaginian way of war comes up against each other in this great titanic clash.
sentences.zh: 他们在描述当罗马和迦太基的战争方式在这场伟大的世纪碰撞中正面交锋时实际发生了什么时，其生动程度异乎寻常。

sentences.en: And they evoke the dust, the stench, the terror, the horror, which even the victors on the day after the battle are kind of struck dumb by it.
sentences.zh: 他们唤起了尘土、恶臭、恐惧和惊骇，甚至连战役结束第二天胜利者都被这一切震得说不出话来。

sentences.en: And I think that it's possible to evoke and make vivid in a way that is not true about other battles in antiquity, something of the lived experience of those who fought in it.
sentences.zh: 我认为，以古代其他战役所不具备的方式，唤起并生动还原那些参战者的亲身经历是完全可能的。

sentences.en: So that's why it's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是它如此有趣的原因。

sentences.en: So we can immerse ourselves in a way that we can't with other battles.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以以前所未有的方式沉浸其中，这是其他战役所做不到的。

sentences.en: We can immerse ourselves in what it was like to be there.
sentences.zh: 我们可以身临其境地去感受当时在那里的经历。

sentences.en: So before we get into the sort of the total immersion, as it were, let's give ourselves a little bit of context.
sentences.zh: 那么，在我们真正进入这种全方位的沉浸体验之前，让我们先了解一下背景。

sentences.en: So Hannibal, listeners will remember, had invaded Italy in autumn 218, this amazing journey across the Alps with his elephants that took two weeks,
sentences.zh: 听众们可能会记得，汉尼拔在公元前218年秋天入侵了意大利，他带着大象翻越阿尔卑斯山，这是一场历时两周的惊人旅程，

sentences.en: then down into the Valley of the Po.
sentences.zh: 随后进入波河河谷。

sentences.en: He had defeated a combined Roman army at the River Trebia.
sentences.zh: 他在特雷比亚河击败了一支罗马联军。

sentences.en: Then six months or so later, the summer of 217, he had ambushed an entire Roman army near Lake Trasimene.
sentences.zh: 大约六个月后，即公元前217年夏天，他在特拉西梅诺湖附近伏击了整整一支罗马军队。

sentences.en: That's seen in the Defile, when all his men are up on the heights and they come pouring down.
sentences.zh: 那是在狭谷中，当时他所有的部下都在高处，然后蜂拥而下。

sentences.en: And they'd killed the consul, who was commanding the Pete Hegseth of the Roman Republic, if you remember.
sentences.zh: 如果你们还记得的话，他们杀死了那位指挥罗马共和国皮特·海格塞斯（Pete Hegseth）的执政官。

sentences.en: He's been roaming around Southern Italy, around Campania, the Roman breadbasket, torching the estates of the Roman nobility.
sentences.zh: 他一直在意大利南部游荡，穿梭于罗马的粮仓坎帕尼亚，烧毁罗马贵族的庄园。

sentences.en: Since then, he has been on the eastern flank of Rome in Apulia.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，他一直位于罗马在阿普利亚的东翼。

sentences.en: It's basically R&R for his men.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是他部下的休假休养时间。

sentences.en: They've been recharging their batteries, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 他们一直在休整，对吧？

sentences.en: So at this point, Tom, what does Hannibal want to do?
sentences.zh: 那么在这一点上，汤姆，汉尼拔想做什么？

sentences.en: What's his plan?
sentences.zh: 他的计划是什么？

sentences.en: To take the city of Rome, to destroy the Roman Republic?
sentences.zh: 是要攻占罗马城，还是摧毁罗马共和国？

sentences.en: No, that's too ambitious for him.
sentences.zh: 不，这对他的野心来说太大了。

sentences.en: So what does he think he's going to plausibly do?
sentences.zh: 那他认为自己切实可行地能做什么呢？

sentences.en: I think that the Romans assume that his ambition is to wipe out Rome.
sentences.zh: 我认为罗马人假设他的野心是消灭罗马。

sentences.en: But I think that they're projecting their own assumptions onto Hannibal there.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们是将自己的假设投射到了汉尼拔身上。

sentences.en: I don't think Hannibal...
sentences.zh: 我不认为汉尼拔……

sentences.en: Well, we know this because later he signs treaties, say, with the King of Macedon, and he specifies what Rome's role will be in this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们知道这一点，因为后来他与马其顿国王等人签署了条约，并具体说明了罗马在其中的角色。

sentences.en: He's not saying that Rome is going to be wiped out.
sentences.zh: 他并没有说罗马会被彻底消灭。

sentences.en: What he wants, essentially, is to destroy the alliance system in Italy that upholds Roman power, and it upholds it because it provides Rome with men.
sentences.zh: 他本质上想要做的是，摧毁意大利境内支撑罗马权力的同盟体系，而这个体系之所以能支撑罗马，是因为它为罗马源源不断地提供兵源。

sentences.en: The whole way through this series, we've been talking, this is the key to Roman power, and Hannibal recognizes that.
sentences.zh: 在这整个系列节目中，我们一直在讨论，这是罗马权力的关键，汉尼拔也意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: And his strategy is to try and kneecap Rome's prestige.
sentences.zh: 他的策略是试图削弱罗马的声望。

sentences.en: And he wants to do that, essentially, by looting and pillaging her lands to demonstrate to everybody that the Romans can no longer defend their own lands.
sentences.zh: 他本质上想通过劫掠和洗劫罗马的土地来做到这一点，向所有人证明罗马人已经无力保卫他们自己的土地。

sentences.en: But above all, he wants to annihilate her armies repeatedly in battle, so that in the long run, the Romans will be forced to sue for terms,
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，他想要在战斗中一次又一次地歼灭罗马军队，这样从长远来看，罗马人将被迫求和，

sentences.en: because this is what people do in antiquity.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是古代人们的做事方式。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians have been fighting wars for centuries and centuries.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人已经打了几个世纪的仗。

sentences.en: It's never been a war of total annihilation.
sentences.zh: 这从来都不是一场彻底歼灭的战争。

sentences.en: It's always been about forcing your enemy to sue for terms, and then you arrive at a kind of compromise, and everyone gets on with their lives.
sentences.zh: 这总是关于迫使你的敌人求和，然后达成某种妥协，大家继续过各自的生活。

sentences.en: It's very Roman to assume that it's all or nothing.
sentences.zh: 认为非此即彼、全盘皆输才是真正的罗马风格。

sentences.en: And this, I think, ultimately is what Hannibal doesn't understand.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这最终正是汉尼拔所不理解的地方。

sentences.en: Perhaps he comes to the understanding of it over the course of his time in Italy.
sentences.zh: 也许他在意大利的经历过程中逐渐意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: But at this point, he still thinks if he can only force the ultimate climactic battle, then he will be able to get the Italians to cast off their loyalty to Rome,
sentences.zh: 但在此时，他仍然认为，只要他能强行引发那场决定性的巅峰之战，他就能够让意大利人抛弃对罗马的忠诚，

sentences.en: to come over to him, and the Romans will be forced to sue for terMs.
sentences.zh: 转而投靠他，而罗马人也将被迫求和。

sentences.en: And, of course, this requires him to tread very delicately on Italian toes.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就要求他在对待意大利人的情感时必须要非常小心谨慎。

sentences.en: So that's one of the reasons why, over the course of the winter, he moves camp so he doesn't outstay his welcome.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是他在整个冬天不断转移营地、以免招致厌烦的原因之一。

sentences.en: And it's why, in the course of the summer of 218, he moves to a specifically Roman depot, a Roman entrepot full of stores and arms, which is called Cannae.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么在公元前218年夏天，他转移到一个专门的罗马军需库——一个储藏着物资和武器、名叫坎尼的罗马转运站。

sentences.en: And he captures this town.
sentences.zh: 他攻占了这座城镇。

sentences.en: All the kind of the material, the weapons, the provender, the produce that are stored there are now Hannibal's.
sentences.zh: 所有储存在那里的物资、武器、粮食和农产品现在都归汉尼拔所有了。

sentences.en: It enables him to cut across Roman supply lines.
sentences.zh: 这使他能够切断罗马的补给线。

sentences.en: It prompts the local Italians to start wavering in their loyalty to Rome, which is everything that Hannibal wants.
sentences.zh: 这促使当地的意大利人开始动摇对罗马的忠诚，而这正是汉尼拔梦寐以求的。

sentences.en: But also there is an additional advantage to it, which is that although Cannae stands on a slight ridge of hills, all around it, the land, and this is quite unusual for Italy,
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还有一个额外的好处，那就是尽管坎尼坐落在一个略微隆起的小山脊上，但它周围的土地——这在意大利相当罕见——

sentences.en: is completely flat.
sentences.zh: 是完全平坦的。

sentences.en: And because it's flat, this makes it perfect for cavalry.
sentences.zh: 正因为地势平坦，这里极其适合骑兵作战。

sentences.en: And cavalry is, in many ways, Hannibal's strongest arm.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，骑兵正是汉尼拔最强大的兵种。

sentences.en: And it's the Roman's weakest arm.
sentences.zh: 而这正是罗马人最薄弱的兵种。

sentences.en: And so he's hoping, I think, to offer himself and his army as bait.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，他希望将自己和军队作为诱饵。

sentences.en: And Cannae is the hook.
sentences.zh: 而坎尼就是鱼钩。

sentences.en: So he wants to lure them into another battle, another pitch battle, because basically he thinks he's unbeatable in pitch battles, do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以他想诱使他们进行另一场战斗，另一场主力决战，因为他基本上认为自己在主力决战中是不可战胜的，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I think he's backing himself.
sentences.zh: 我认为他对自己充满信心。

sentences.en: I think, you know, backing himself all the way.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道的，他对自己的胜算全盘押注。

sentences.en: But he, you know, also he recognises it's the only way he has any prospect of winning.
sentences.zh: 但他也知道，这是他赢得战争的唯一希望所在。

sentences.en: I mean, he's right in that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这点上他是对的。

sentences.en: He just has to beat them again and again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 他必须一次、一次、又一次、又一次地击败他们。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So what about the Romans?
sentences.zh: 那么罗马人呢？

sentences.en: Are they going to take this trap?
sentences.zh: 他们会上这个钩吗？

sentences.en: Because if you remember from last time, Fabius Maximus, who had been serving as dictator, he'd been appointed for six months as sort of supreme magistrate,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你还记得上次的内容，曾担任独裁官的费边·马克西姆斯（Fabius Maximus）曾被任命为拥有最高行政长官权力、为期六个月的独裁官，

sentences.en: the man who makes the decisions in command of the republic.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个掌握共和国最高指挥权并做出决定的人。

sentences.en: He has been actually shying away from battle.
sentences.zh: 他其实一直在避战。

sentences.en: I mean, his whole strategy has been wait and see, play the long game.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的整个策略就是以静制动、放长线钓大鱼。

sentences.en: Delaying.
sentences.zh: 拖延战术。

sentences.en: The Fabian strategy.
sentences.zh: 费边策略。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You said last time that a lot of the Romans don't like this.
sentences.zh: 你上次说过，许多罗马人并不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: They think it's un-Roman.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这不符合罗马的作风。

sentences.en: They're losing patience.
sentences.zh: 他们正在失去耐心。

sentences.en: So have they now definitively run out of patience by the time Hannibal sets up his base at Cannae?
sentences.zh: 那么，在汉尼拔在坎尼建立基地的时候，他们的耐心是否已经彻底耗尽了？

sentences.en: Well, I think we said in the last episode, Fabius' strategy, you know, it's not a long-term one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我们在上一集里说过，费边的策略，你知道的，并不是长久之计。

sentences.en: It's all about giving the republic time to recruit and to train and to arm enough men to provide an army that will be so overwhelming that Hannibal will be powerless to defeat it.
sentences.zh: 这完全是为了给共和国争取时间去招募、训练和武装足够多的士兵，从而组建一支压倒性强大、让汉尼拔无力击败的军队。

sentences.en: And the emblem of the fact that the time of emergency is over and it's time to resume normal service and basically launch a war of destruction against the invader
sentences.zh: 而标志着紧急状态已经结束、是时候恢复正常服务并基本上对侵略者发动一场毁灭之战的象征

sentences.en: is the fact that when Fabius lays down his dictatorship, he's only dictated for six months.
sentences.zh: 正是这样一个事实：当费边卸任其独裁官职务时，他实际上只独裁了六个月。

sentences.en: That's the legal restriction.
sentences.zh: 这是法律上的限制。

sentences.en: There are new elections and two new consuls are elected.
sentences.zh: 将会有新的选举，并选出两位新执政官。

sentences.en: And these consuls, certainly one of them, has definitely been elected on a kind of let's defeat Hannibal and, you know, wipe him out in a battle ticket.
sentences.zh: 而这些执政官中，至少其中一位，绝对是带着一种“让我们击败汉尼拔，你知道的，在一场战斗中彻底消灭他”的竞选纲领当选的。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Gaius Torrentius Varro.
sentences.zh: 这个人名叫盖乌斯·特伦蒂乌斯·瓦罗。

sentences.en: He is cast by both Polybius and Livy as being a bit like Flaminius, the guy who had lost the battle at Lake Trasamine.
sentences.zh: 在波利比乌斯和李维的笔下，他被塑造成有点像弗拉米尼乌斯那样的人——那个曾在特拉西梅诺湖战役中惨败的家伙。

sentences.en: So he is cast as a kind of slightly MAGA figure.
sentences.zh: 所以他被塑造成了一个有点类似MAGA（让美国再次伟大）风格的人物。

sentences.en: He's a novice homo.
sentences.zh: 他是一个初出茅庐的新人。

sentences.en: So he's someone from outside the mainstream, outside the conventional political elites.
sentences.zh: 因此，他是一个来自主流之外、传统政治精英之外的人。

sentences.en: And according to Livy, he's actually the son of a butcher, which I think is improbable, probably reflects Livy's snobbery about people who arise above their station.
sentences.zh: 根据李维的说法，他实际上是一个屠夫的儿子，我觉得这不太可能，这可能反映了李维对于那些出身低微却爬上高位的人的势利眼光。

sentences.en: Because clearly, Varro is a very able politician.
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，瓦罗是一位能力极强的政治家。

sentences.en: He actually comes top of the whole roster of people who are campaigning to be consul that year.
sentences.zh: 在当年所有竞选执政官候选人的名单中，他实际上名列榜首。

sentences.en: And it means that the guy who subsequently comes to be elected as his colleague, a guy called Lucius Aemilius Paulus, although he's from a very distinguished political dynasty,
sentences.zh: 这意味着后来当选为他同僚的那个人——一个名叫卢修斯·埃米利乌斯·保卢斯的人，尽管他出身于一个非常显赫的政治世族，
zh_words: 卢修斯·埃米利乌斯·保卢斯

sentences.en: so much more of a conventional consul, he can't really pull rank.
sentences.zh: 更像是一个传统的执政官，但他其实无法压制瓦罗。

sentences.en: Because Varro does have the kind of weight of electoral achievement behind him.
sentences.zh: 因为瓦罗确实有着选举胜利带来的分量在背后支撑。

sentences.en: And it's this that enables Polybius and Livy to cast Varro as the guy who's really responsible for the whole strategy.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，波利比乌斯和李维才得以将瓦罗塑造成真正应对整个战略负责的人。

sentences.en: So Polybius in particular casts him as being rash, as being incompetent, as being headstrong.
sentences.zh: 因此，波利比乌斯尤其将他刻画为轻率、无能且固执己见的人。

sentences.en: And in part, I think this is because clearly Varro was, to a degree.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，我认为瓦罗在某种程度上确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我们将看到的。

sentences.en: But it's also because Aemilius Paulus, the other consul, is the grandfather of Polybius's Roman patron.
sentences.zh: 但这也是因为另一位执政官埃米利乌斯·保卢斯，是波利比乌斯罗马赞助人的祖父。

sentences.en: Oh, so Polybius isn't really going to diss Paulus.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以波利比乌斯其实不会去贬低保卢斯。

sentences.en: And Polybius is keen to spare Paulus' responsibility for this strategy.
sentences.zh: 而且波利比乌斯急于免除保卢斯对这项战略应承担的责任。

sentences.en: And Livy also plays it up, casting Paulus as a man who is very sensible, very balanced, very restrained.
sentences.zh: 李维也极力渲染这一点，将保卢斯塑造为一个非常明智、非常平衡、非常克制的人。

sentences.en: But I think that this is nonsense.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这简直是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: So as with Trebia, I think that both consuls are absolutely set on forcing a battle.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像对特雷比亚战役一样，我认为两位执政官都绝对坚决要强行发起会战。

sentences.en: Because why else would they have raised their forces?
sentences.zh: 因为如果不是这样，他们为什么要组建军队？

sentences.en: Why else would they have marched against Hannibal?
sentences.zh: 如果不是这样，他们为什么要向汉尼拔进军？

sentences.en: Or why would they go against everything that is instinctual in the Roman cast of mind?
sentences.zh: 或者他们为什么要违背罗马人心态中所有出于本能的东西？

sentences.en: And, you know, the reasons that they are set on this course is because they think if they don't wipe out Hannibal, then it absolutely does threaten their hold on Italy.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们之所以执意采取这一方针，是因为他们认为如果不消灭汉尼拔，绝对会威胁到他们对意大利的控制。

sentences.en: But also they feel it as a massive insult.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他们也觉得这是极大的侮辱。

sentences.en: You know, the Romans do not want to be disrespected.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，罗马人绝不希望被人不尊重。

sentences.en: And also they know that if they defeat Hannibal, then that's it.
sentences.zh: 并且他们也知道，只要击败汉尼拔，那就万事大吉了。

sentences.en: Hannibal can't, you know, the Romans can survive endless defeats.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔无法——你知道的，罗马人可以承受无数次的失败。

sentences.en: Hannibal can't.
sentences.zh: 而汉尼拔承受不起。

sentences.en: One defeat for Hannibal and the war is over.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔只要遭遇一次失败，战争就结束了。

sentences.en: So I think all of those reasons, you can see why they think that the Fabian strategy served its time.
sentences.zh: 所以我想出于所有这些原因，你可以理解为什么他们认为费边的战略已经完成了它的历史使命。

sentences.en: But now, enough.
sentences.zh: 但现在，够了。

sentences.en: Let's crack on.
sentences.zh: 让我们大干一场吧。

sentences.en: Let's do this.
sentences.zh: 让我们行动起来。

sentences.en: And they've had a long time to think about it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们已经花了很长时间来考虑这件事。

sentences.en: I mean, months and months have passed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几个月又几个月过去了。

sentences.en: They've had a long time to think about,
sentences.zh: 他们有很长时间来思考：

sentences.en: OK, here is this guy with all his cavalry and whatnot, the Africans, the Gauls and stuff.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是那个带着他所有的骑兵什么的家伙，非洲人、高卢人等等。

sentences.en: How are we actually going to beat him?
sentences.zh: 我们到底该怎么打败他？

sentences.en: And Tom, have they dreamed up a new, effective strategy?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他们有没有想出一个新的、有效的战略？

sentences.en: Well, we mentioned the Battle of the Somme.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们提到了索姆河战役。

sentences.en: And I know that there's kind of revisionist takes on British First World War generals.
sentences.zh: 我知道现在对英国第一次世界大战将领有一种修正主义的看法。

sentences.en: But I think there is a slight element of, you know, the conventional idea that, oh, that didn't work.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这其中多少有点那种传统观点的影子，也就是：“哦，那招没用。”

sentences.en: Let's try it again, only with more men.
sentences.zh: “让我们再试一次，只不过要投入更多的人手。”

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's basically what's happening.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is because the ability to raise enormous numbers of men is what the Roman Republic is all about.
sentences.zh: 之所以会这样，是因为能够动员数量庞大的人员正是罗马共和国的看家本领。

sentences.en: And clearly, it's something that Hannibal can't do.
sentences.zh: 显然，这也是汉尼拔所做不到的。

sentences.en: So the aim is to just raise an army that is so vast that there is no prospect of it possibly losing.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们的目标就是组建一支如此庞大的军队，以至于根本不可能有战败的前景。

sentences.en: So what they do is there are four legions already in the field.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的做法是，前线已经有四个军团。

sentences.en: So there were the two legions that had been left in the field after late Trasamine under the command of the consul who hadn't been wiped out, which Fabius had then taken over.
sentences.zh: 也就是特拉西梅诺湖战役后留在前线的两个军团，当时由未被全歼的那位执政官指挥，后来由费边接管。

sentences.en: And he had then recruited two further legions.
sentences.zh: 接着他又征集了另外两个军团。

sentences.en: So that's four legions.
sentences.zh: 所以那是四个军团。

sentences.en: And they have been sent off at the beginning of 218 to shadow Hannibal on the eastern side of the Apennines in Apulia.
sentences.zh: 他们在公元前218年之初就被派往亚平宁山脉东侧的普利亚，去跟踪监视汉尼拔。

sentences.en: So they are already in situ.
sentences.zh: 所以他们已经就位了。

sentences.en: Paulus and Varro, the two new consuls, they then set about raising two new legions each.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯和瓦罗，这两位新执政官，随后着手每人各组建两个新军团。

sentences.en: So another four in total.
sentences.zh: 因此总共又是四个军团。

sentences.en: And they spend the early months of their consulship drilling them, training them, readying them for battle.
sentences.zh: 他们将执政官任期的头几个月花在对这些军团进行操练、训练和为战斗做准备上。

sentences.en: Now, these legions are much larger than normal.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些军团的规模比平常大得多。

sentences.en: So each one consists of 5,000 infantry, 300 cavalry.
sentences.zh: 因此每个军团包含5000名步兵、300名骑兵。

sentences.en: They also recruit an equal number of men from the Italian allies.
sentences.zh: 他们还从意大利盟友中征集了同等数量的人员。

sentences.en: So mental maths, the total is about 80,000 infantry, 6,000 cavalry.
sentences.zh: 所以用心算一下，总数大约是8万名步兵、6000名骑兵。

sentences.en: I mean, 80,000 infantry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，8万名步兵。

sentences.en: I mean, that is an enormous number of men.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一个庞大得惊人的数字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: By any standards, let alone the standards of the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 无论按什么标准来看，更不用说古代世界的标准了。

sentences.en: That's about twice the size of Villa Park.
sentences.zh: 这大约是维拉公园球场容量的两倍。

sentences.en: Oh, my word.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: That's your standard.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的衡量标准。

sentences.en: That is literally almost as many people as there are members of the Restos History Club.
sentences.zh: 这简直跟“雷斯托历史俱乐部”的会员人数差不多快一样多了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是相当多的人。

sentences.en: Imagine them all being wiped out.
sentences.zh: 想象一下他们全部被歼灭。

sentences.en: That would be terrible.
sentences.zh: 那将是可怕的。

sentences.en: Yeah, awful.
sentences.zh: 是的，太惨烈了。

sentences.en: I mean, what a formidable force they would make.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一支多么令人生畏的力量啊。

sentences.en: Let's be serious about it.
sentences.zh: 让我们严肃地对待这件事。

sentences.en: This is now a force far bigger than anything Hannibal can command, right?
sentences.zh: 这现在是一支远比汉尼拔所能指挥的任何军队都要庞大的力量，对吧？

sentences.en: So they have good grounds for thinking, you know, no matter what the tactics, our army is now so enormous.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有充分的理由认为，不管战术如何，我们的军队现在如此庞大。

sentences.en: There's no way Hannibal can beat us.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔绝无可能击败我们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this sense that the whole city is now going to war is enhanced by the fact that about a third of the Senate are serving in the army.
sentences.zh: 整个城市现在都要开赴战场的感觉，由于大约三分之一的元老院成员都在军队中服役而得到了进一步的强化。

sentences.en: And this sense that the Roman elites justify their status by their readiness to fight is very, very manifest in the roster of people going to war with Hannibal in 216.
sentences.zh: 罗马精英通过随时准备战斗来证明其地位正当性的这种意识，在公元前216年随汉尼拔出征的人员名单中表现得非常、非常明显。

sentences.en: Fabius doesn't go, but his erstwhile master of horse, Minicius Rufus, he goes, he's serving as a tribune.
sentences.zh: 费边没有去，但他从前的骑兵长官米尼基乌斯·鲁夫斯去了，他作为一名军事保民官在服役。

sentences.en: So are many others who have been consuls, so they have experience of command.
sentences.zh: 许多其他曾担任过执政官的人也是如此，所以他们拥有指挥经验。

sentences.en: They're all serving as tribunes who are essentially the kind of the link men between the two consuls who are in command and the mass of the legions.
sentences.zh: 他们都在担任军事保民官，这基本上相当于身居指挥地位的两名执政官与广大军团士兵之间的纽带人员。

sentences.en: You know, it's not just about the vastness of the manpower.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不仅仅关乎庞大的人力。

sentences.en: It's also about the seasoned experience of the commanding officers.
sentences.zh: 这也关乎指挥官们身经百战的丰富经验。

sentences.en: And these officers, for the first time in Roman history, swear a formal oath of service, what's called a sacramentum.
sentences.zh: 而这些军官在罗马历史上第一次宣誓效忠的正式誓言，也就是所谓的“萨克拉门图姆”。

sentences.en: And Livy gives us the terms of it, never to leave the field in order to save their own skins,
sentences.zh: 李维为我们提供了誓词的内容：为了保全自己的性命绝不离开战场，

sentences.en: nor to abandon their place in the line for any purpose other than to recover or fetch a weapon, to strike an enemy or to save a friend.
sentences.zh: 也绝不为了除取回或寻找武器、打击敌人或拯救战友之外的任何目的而放弃他们在战线中的位置。

sentences.en: And this will establish a template for the oath that, you know, soldiers are swearing when they join the legions for centuries to come.
sentences.zh: 这将为几个世纪以来士兵们加入军团时所宣誓的誓言确立一个模板。

sentences.en: It's all about fostering a sense of common purpose, that this really is the Roman people in arms, joined in a unity,
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了培养一种共同目标的意识，即这确实是拿起武器的罗马人民，团结在一起，

sentences.en: in a kind of sense of determination that is shared by every class of person, by every age group.
sentences.zh: 带着一种为各个阶层、各个年龄段的人所共有的坚定决心。

sentences.en: And I think this matters not just for psychological reasons, but also because there is a slight problem with the sheer scale of the army, which is that it's not at all integrated.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不仅出于心理层面的原因，还因为这支庞大军队的绝对规模本身存在一个小问题，那就是它完全没有经过磨合。

sentences.en: I mean, none of these legions have kind of really served with each other.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些军团之前基本上都没有并肩作战过。

sentences.en: So Varro and Paulus, they each have their own two legions.
sentences.zh: 所以瓦罗和保卢斯，他们各自拥有自己的两个军团。

sentences.en: Then you've got the four legions that are on a century north of Cannae.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有驻扎在卡奈以北一个世纪（注：原文如此）的那四个军团。

sentences.en: None of these legions have trained or still less campaigned together.
sentences.zh: 这些军团从未一起训练过，更不用说一起进行军事战役了。

sentences.en: And the consequence of that, of course, is that in a sense, the very size of the army becomes a source of potential weakness as well as of strength, because it's very ponderous.
sentences.zh: 其结果当然就是，从某种意义上说，军队的庞大本身既成为了潜力的弱点之源，也成为了力量之源，因为它实在太笨重了。

sentences.en: It's very muscle bound.
sentences.zh: 它显得有些尾大不掉。

sentences.en: It doesn't have the ability to do complicated manoeuvres or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 它没有能力执行复杂的机动或类似的事情。

sentences.en: It can only do the most basic tactics.
sentences.zh: 它只能执行最基本的战术。

sentences.en: And Hannibal knows this.
sentences.zh: 而汉尼拔深知这一点。

sentences.en: You know, his spies will be out there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他的密探会散布出去。

sentences.en: He will be computing and working it out.
sentences.zh: 他会进行计算并把这一切琢磨透。

sentences.en: And I think that that's why you have this incredible scene in late July,
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么在七月下旬会出现这样令人难以置信的场景，

sentences.en: when at last the two consuls have joined the other four legions north of Cannae and then advancing southwards towards Cannae, where Hannibal's army is.
sentences.zh: 当时两位执政官终于与卡奈以北的其他四个军团会合，然后向南朝着汉尼拔军队所在的卡奈进发。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginians, like the Spartans at Thermopylae, seeing the Persians approach,
sentences.zh: 迦太基人就像温泉关的斯巴达人看到波斯人逼近一样，

sentences.en: they see great dust clouds kicking up and then the glint of metal and this army that is vast beyond their wildest imaginings.
sentences.zh: 他们看到腾空而起的滚滚尘土，接着是金属的闪光，以及这支超乎他们最大胆想象的庞大军队。

sentences.en: And it's not surprising that a lot of the Carthaginians feel quite nervous.
sentences.zh: 许多迦太基人感到相当紧张，这也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: And there's an anecdote that's recorded by Plutarch.
sentences.zh: 普鲁塔克记录了一则轶事。

sentences.en: And there's one of Hannibal's officers, a guy named Gisco, expressed himself astonished by the numbers of the enemy.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔的一位军官，一个名叫吉斯科的人，对敌人的人数之多表示了惊奇。

sentences.en: Hannibal adopted a serious expression and said, yes, Gisco, but you are overlooking an even more astonishing fact.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔面色凝重地说：“是的，吉斯科，但你忽视了一个更令人惊奇的事实。”

sentences.en: And what is that?
sentences.zh: “那是什么？”

sentences.en: Asked Gisco.
sentences.zh: 吉斯科问道。

sentences.en: Why, answered Hannibal, that in all that vast Roman army, there is no one called Gisco.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔回答：“嗨，在所有那庞大的罗马军队里，竟然没有一个人叫吉斯科。”

sentences.en: And there is manly laughter.
sentences.zh: 接着是一阵充满男子气概的笑声。

sentences.en: I actually genuinely don't get what he's talking about.
sentences.zh: 我其实真心没听懂他在说什么。

sentences.en: What's his point?
sentences.zh: 他的重点是什么？

sentences.en: He's saying, OK, they have all these numbers, but they don't have anyone.
sentences.zh: 他是说，好吧，他们人多势众，但他们没有人才。

sentences.en: You know, they don't have people of your calibre, Gisco.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们没有像你这样 calibre（水平）的人，吉斯科。

sentences.en: I am surrounded by people like you.
sentences.zh: 我身边都是像你这样的人。

sentences.en: We have the winning of this.
sentences.zh: 我们赢定这场战争了。

sentences.en: And I think that that anecdote kind of sums up what seems to have been the mood, probably on both sides,
sentences.zh: 我认为那则轶事在某种程度上概括了当时双方的心理状态，

sentences.en: which is a kind of a mixture of nervousness and confidence of kind of hesitancy, but also a kind of relish for the big showdown, the World Cup final that is approaching.
sentences.zh: 那是一种既紧张又自信、既有些犹豫却又对即将到来的那场像世界杯决赛似的大对决充满渴望的混合情绪。

sentences.en: Everyone knows this is the big one.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道这是一场重头戏。

sentences.en: And I think that probably explains why battle isn't joined immediately.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概可以解释为什么双方没有立即开战。

sentences.en: There's a certain degree of eyeballing.
sentences.zh: 这里面有某种程度的互不相让、用眼神较量。

sentences.en: You know, it's the two heavyweight champions kind of standing on the weights and, you know, insulting each other and that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像两个重量级拳王站在称重台上，然后你知道的，互相羞辱之类的。

sentences.en: So one will draw up battle lines, but the other won't respond.
sentences.zh: 所以一方会摆好战阵，但另一方不会回应。

sentences.en: Then the other will do it.
sentences.zh: 接着另一方照做。

sentences.en: They're kind of maneuvering this way and that.
sentences.zh: 他们就这样来来回回地调兵遣将。

sentences.en: And Polybius and Livy, when they look back at this, they say, oh, well, this is because Paulus is in command one day and he doesn't want to fight.
sentences.zh: 而波利比乌斯和李维在回溯这段历史时会说，哦，这是因为保卢斯有一天在指挥，他不想打仗。

sentences.en: And then Barrow is the next day and he's eager to fight.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天轮到瓦罗，他渴望开战。

sentences.en: I don't think that's true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不是真的。

sentences.en: I think it's reflective of, you know, the mixture of anticipation and nervousness that is characteristic on both sides.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了双方普遍存在的那种期待与紧张交织的心态。

sentences.en: They're kind of tensing themselves up, but it's perfectly clear there is going to be a battle because there's no way that either side can back down.
sentences.zh: 他们正在积蓄力量严阵以待，但非常显而易见的是，一场大战势在必行，因为双方都绝无退缩的可能。

sentences.en: And sure enough, Dominic, on the 2nd of August, 2.16, Dawn sees the Romans taking up positions to offer battle and Hannibal rides out to a ridge, looks at it,
sentences.zh: 果不其然，多米尼克，在公元前216年8月2日，黎明见证了罗马人摆好阵势准备迎战，而汉尼拔骑马来到一处山脊上，看了一眼，

sentences.en: gives the signal to his men, his general staff who are around him, says, yeah, let's go for this.
sentences.zh: 向他身边的部下和总参谋部人员发出信号，说道：“好，我们上吧。”

sentences.en: And it becomes clear to the Romans that Hannibal is going to accept their offer of battle.
sentences.zh: 罗马人清楚地看到汉尼拔将接受他们的战斗邀约。
