sentences.en: It is dawn on the 2nd of August, 216.
sentences.zh: 公元前216年8月2日黎明。

sentences.en: I'm outside the tent of the Roman commander, Varro.
sentences.zh: 我正站在罗马指挥官瓦罗的帐篷外。

sentences.en: A red flag has been hoisted.
sentences.zh: 一面红旗已经升起。

sentences.en: The signal, Tom, that battle is about to begin.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这就是战斗即将打响的信号。

sentences.en: So paint the scene for us, please.
sentences.zh: 请为我们描绘一下当时的场景。

sentences.en: So the senior Roman officers have already met for their briefing.
sentences.zh: 罗马高级军官们已经开过作战会议了。

sentences.en: And they've gone out to tell their men what the plan is.
sentences.zh: 他们已经出去向士兵们传达作战计划。

sentences.en: The two consuls, Varro and Paulus, have emerged from their headquarters.
sentences.zh: 两位执政官，瓦罗和保卢斯，从他们的指挥部里走了出来。

sentences.en: And they are wearing the traditional scarlet cloak that a consul wears on a day of battle.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着执政官在战斗之日穿的传统绯红色斗篷。

sentences.en: So this is not the Trebia where Hannibal had bounced the Romans into fighting without having breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像特雷比亚战役，当时汉尼拔在罗马人连早饭都没吃的时候就激怒他们开战。

sentences.en: This time, the Romans have all breakfasted and then leaving camp, they've been able to take up position on ground of their own generals choosing.
sentences.zh: 这一次，罗马人吃过早饭才离开军营，并且能够在他们将军们选择的地形上列阵。

sentences.en: Now, it has always been a problem for us doing podcasts about battles.
sentences.zh: 制作关于战役的播客对我们来说一直是个难题。

sentences.en: Firstly, that it's quite difficult to paint the scene on a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 首先，在播客里描绘战场场景相当困难。

sentences.en: And secondly, that sometimes we're not quite as interested in military dispositions as we should be.
sentences.zh: 其次，有时我们对军事部署的关注度可能不如应有的那么高。

sentences.en: However, this for me is an exception because this is the one battle that I've been obsessed by since I was very young.
sentences.zh: 然而，对我和说这绝对是个例外，因为这是我从小就着迷的一场战役。

sentences.en: And I had a book by a brilliant writer and artist called Peter Connolly.
sentences.zh: 我有一本由才华横溢的作家兼插画家彼得·康诺利写的书。

sentences.en: And he wrote a series, one on the Romans, one on the Greek armies.
sentences.zh: 他写了一个系列，一本关于罗马人，一本关于希腊军队。

sentences.en: And then he wrote one called Hannibal and the Enemies of Rome, which I still have it right next to me as I sit here.
sentences.zh: 然后他又写了一本叫《汉尼拔与罗马的敌人》，我坐在这里时，它就放在我手边。

sentences.en: And he did the illustrations for it as well as writing the text.
sentences.zh: 书中的插图和文字都是他自己完成的。

sentences.en: And his take was that, I'll set the scene, there is this very flat featureless plane,
sentences.zh: 他的看法是，我来描述一下场景，这里是一片非常平坦、没有任何地貌特征的平原，

sentences.en: but there are two natural features that determined where Connolly thinks the battle was fought.
sentences.zh: 但有两个自然特征决定了康诺利认为战役发生的位置。

sentences.en: The first of these is a very winding river called the Alphidius, the course of which has changed over the course of time.
sentences.zh: 其中第一个是一条名为阿尔菲迪乌斯的蜿蜒河流，它的河道随着时间推移发生了变化。

sentences.en: But Connolly argues that it was about one and a half miles from a ridge of hills.
sentences.zh: 但康诺利认为，它距离一处山脊大约有一英里半。

sentences.en: And Cannae sits on this ridge of hills.
sentences.zh: 坎尼就坐落在这个山脊上。

sentences.en: And so you have this stretch of open ground between the hills and the river Alphidius.
sentences.zh: 因此，在山脊和阿尔菲迪乌斯河之间有这样一片开阔地。

sentences.en: And to quote Goldsworthy, who buys into Connolly's take on this, the advantages of this position are obvious.
sentences.zh: 用赞同康诺利看法的戈德史密斯的话来说，这个位置的优势显而易见。

sentences.en: The Romans were able to anchor one flank on the river and the other on the high ground near Cannae,
sentences.zh: 罗马人能够将一翼依托在河畔，另一翼依托在坎尼附近的高地上，

sentences.en: making it impossible for the Carthaginian horse to envelop their line as they had at Trebia.
sentences.zh: 这使得迦太基骑兵无法像在特雷比亚那样包抄他们的阵线。

sentences.en: So I hope that makes sense to the listeners.
sentences.zh: 希望听众们能听明白这一点。

sentences.en: Right, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 没错，这很好理解。

sentences.en: If you think, the Romans come out and on their left flank, you have a ridge of hills and on their right flank, you have a river.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想，罗马人出营后，左翼是山脊，右翼是河流。

sentences.en: And this means that it's harder for the Carthaginians to outflank them with their cavalry.
sentences.zh: 这意味着迦太基人很难用骑兵对他们实施迂回包抄。

sentences.en: Yeah, so they're stretched across the terrain and they can't possibly be encircled.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他们横跨地形展开，绝无被合围的可能。

sentences.en: So there's a further advantage, which is that they're not staring into the sun because they're essentially facing kind of roughly southwards.
sentences.zh: 还有一个优势，就是他们不会迎着阳光，因为他们基本上大致朝南面对战场。

sentences.en: There is one issue, which is that the wind is whipping up the duSt.
sentences.zh: 不过还有一个问题，那就是风卷起了尘土。

sentences.en: It's kind of late July in southern Italy.
sentences.zh: 当时是意大利南部七月下旬。

sentences.en: So there's quite a lot of dust and kind of blowing it into their faces.
sentences.zh: 所以尘土相当大，直往他们脸吹。

sentences.en: But I think Varro clearly feels that the advantage of the position outweighs that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为瓦罗显然觉得这个位置的优势盖过了这个缺点。

sentences.en: So his dispositions, infantry in the middle, as ever, Roman cavalry on his right wing.
sentences.zh: 所以他的部署是：步兵居中，一如既往，罗马骑兵在他的右翼。

sentences.en: So that's next to the Alphidius, next to the river.
sentences.zh: 也就是靠近阿尔菲迪乌斯河的那一边。

sentences.en: And then the Allied cavalry is on the left wing, which is next to the Ridge of Hills.
sentences.zh: 同盟国骑兵则在左翼，靠近山脊。

sentences.en: And their role is purely defensive.
sentences.zh: 他们的任务纯粹是防守。

sentences.en: You know, they're always going to be outnumbered and outfought by the Carthaginian horse.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们在数量和战斗力上始终会处于劣势，不如迦太基骑兵。

sentences.en: Their role is essentially to ensure that the line of infantry can't be attacked on the flanks.
sentences.zh: 他们的核心任务其实是确保步兵阵线不会遭到侧翼袭击。

sentences.en: And this is really, really important because the goal has to be that the infantry defeats the Carthaginian infantry before the Roman and Italian cavalry can be chased off.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常非常重要，因为目标必须是让步兵在罗马和意大利骑兵被驱逐之前击败迦太基步兵。

sentences.en: And it's the measure of how important this is that Varro himself takes up command of the Allied cavalry and Paulus leads the Roman cavalry.
sentences.zh: 从瓦罗亲自指挥同盟国骑兵、保卢斯率领罗马骑兵这一点，就能看出这有多重要。

sentences.en: So very, very important.
sentences.zh: 所以这至关重要。

sentences.en: But obviously, it's the infantry that the Romans are pinning their hopes on.
sentences.zh: 但显然，罗马人是将希望寄托在步兵身上的。

sentences.en: And so we should probably just describe, you know, what they look like, how they're lined up, how they're armed, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们或许应该描述一下，你知道的，他们的外表、阵型、武器装备，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Because these are not legions, not Roman soldiers of the kind that most people will be familiar with from Gladiator or whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为这些并不是军团，不是大多数人通过《角斗士》或其他作品所熟知的那种罗马士兵。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is from a kind of earlier period.
sentences.zh: 这是来自一个更早时期的军队。

sentences.en: And essentially, the Roman infantry is lined up in four distinct ranks.
sentences.zh: 本质上，罗马步兵排成四个清晰的纵列。

sentences.en: So the first line consists of very lightly armed skirmishers who are called valites.
sentences.zh: 第一线由装备轻便的散兵组成，被称为“轻步兵”（velites）。

sentences.en: And Polybius specifies that these are the youngest and the pooreSt.
sentences.zh: 波利比乌斯明确指出，这些人是最年轻、最贫穷的。

sentences.en: He gives a kind of very detailed account of how the Romans fought in battles.
sentences.zh: 他对罗马人在战斗中的作战方式进行了非常详细的描述。

sentences.en: Very groovily, they would often wear wolf skin.
sentences.zh: 非常酷炫的是，他们经常身穿狼皮。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, you have your little spears and you have your wolf skin and you form a screen in front of the main block of the heavy infantry.
sentences.zh: 对，你们拿着小标枪，身穿狼皮，在重步兵主力部队前方形成一道防御屏障。

sentences.en: And they form three lines.
sentences.zh: 他们排成三线。

sentences.en: So the first line is a group called Hastati.
sentences.zh: 第一线是一群被称为“青年兵”（Hastati）的人。

sentences.en: These are men in their late teens, early 20s.
sentences.zh: 这些人正值十多岁到二十岁出头。

sentences.en: So they're young, they're full of vigor, but they're not as experienced as the next line of heavy infantry who are called the principes.
sentences.zh: 所以他们年轻、充满活力，但不如下一线重步兵经验丰富，后者被称为“壮年兵”（principes）。

sentences.en: So the chief men, these are guys who are in the prime of life.
sentences.zh: 也就是精锐骨干，这些人正值盛年。

sentences.en: They're very fit.
sentences.zh: 他们体魄极佳。

sentences.en: They're very strong, but they're also experienced.
sentences.zh: 他们非常强壮，同时也很有经验。

sentences.en: And then at the back, you have a line called the triarii who are the veterans.
sentences.zh: 然后在最后面，是一条被称为“老兵”（triarii）的防线。

sentences.en: Now, how are these heavy infantry armed?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些重步兵是如何武装的呢？

sentences.en: It's quite important for understanding the battle to get a sense of this.
sentences.zh: 了解这一点对于理解这场战役非常重要。

sentences.en: All the heavy infantry have very heavy kind of large oblong shields, which are held up with the left arm.
sentences.zh: 所有的重步兵都装备了非常沉重的大型长方形盾牌，用左臂托着。

sentences.en: So that's quite a strain on the arm over the course of a long day.
sentences.zh: 因此在漫长的一天中，这对手臂来说是相当大的负担。

sentences.en: They might have a kind of small oblong plate on their chest, the pectorale, or if they can afford it, chain mail.
sentences.zh: 他们的胸前可能会有一块小型长方形护胸板，即胸甲（pectorale），如果买得起的话，也可以穿锁子甲。

sentences.en: And they're armed with the Spanish stabbing sword.
sentences.zh: 他们配备了西班牙短刺剑。

sentences.en: So the sword that opens up the guts of the person that you're fighting with, you know, if you can get a clear stab at him.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你能准确刺中的话，这把剑能剖开与你交战之人的内脏。

sentences.en: So the front two ranks, so that's the hastati and the principes, they also have two javelins.
sentences.zh: 因此，前两线——也就是青年兵和壮年兵——还配有两支标枪。

sentences.en: And I'll just quote Goldsworthy on this because lots of people listening to this have a sense that these javelins, the pilar,
sentences.zh: 我在这里引用一下戈德史密斯的话，因为许多听众觉得这些标枪（即皮鲁姆标枪），

sentences.en: the legionaries throw them and they then have a kind of bendy head.
sentences.zh: 军团士兵投掷它们，然后它们的枪头是会弯曲的。

sentences.en: It's meant to stick in the enemy's shield and the droops down.
sentences.zh: 这是为了卡在敌人的盾牌上然后垂下来。

sentences.en: This is not true.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: I'll read Goldsworthy on how these javelins work.
sentences.zh: 我来读读戈德史密斯关于这些标枪如何发挥作用的描述。

sentences.en: All of the weapon's weight was concentrated behind the small tip, giving it great penetrative power.
sentences.zh: 武器的全部重量都集中在小巧的尖端后面，使其具有极强的穿透力。

sentences.en: The length of the metal shank gave it the reach to punch through an enemy's shield and still go on to wound his body.
sentences.zh: 金属杆的长度使其能够穿透敌人的盾牌并继续伤害其身体。

sentences.en: But even if it failed to do so and merely stuck in the shield, it was very difficult to pull free and might force the man to discard his weighed down shield and fight unprotected.
sentences.zh: 但即使未能做到这一点而仅仅卡在盾牌上，也很难将其拔出，这可能会迫使敌方士兵丢弃沉重的盾牌，并在毫无保护的情况下作战。

sentences.en: So basically you don't need the head to bend.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上你根本不需要枪头弯曲。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, you know, it's a massive problem if you've got a great spear stuck in your shield.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你想想，如果有一根巨大的长矛卡在你的盾牌上，这就是个天大的麻烦。

sentences.en: You have to throw it away and then the guy can come up with his gladius and slice your stomach open.
sentences.zh: 你不得不把它扔掉，然后对方就可以拿着短剑过来切开你的肚子。

sentences.en: So very bad news.
sentences.zh: 所以这是个绝对糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: The third rank, so this is the veterans, the triarii, they have very long thrusting spears and they essentially are reserved.
sentences.zh: 第三线，也就是老兵，即三线兵，他们拥有非常长的刺矛，基本上作为预备队。

sentences.en: Should the first two ranks break, then they will form a kind of porcupine, a defensive screen bristling with spears.
sentences.zh: 如果前两线被突破，他们就会组成一个刺猬阵，也就是布满长矛的防御屏障。

sentences.en: I'm aware that that might all sound rather complicated, but the aim of it is to enable fresh units constantly to be filtered up to the front.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来可能相当复杂，但其目的是让生力军能够源源不断地被替换到最前线。

sentences.en: So that if one line gets kind of annihilated or loses energy or whatever, then they can easily be replaced.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，如果某条防线被全歼、体力耗尽或遭遇其他情况，他们就能轻松得到补充。

sentences.en: And what gives the Roman line its flexibility is that there are kind of gaps built into the battle formations.
sentences.zh: 赋予罗马阵线灵活性的是其战斗阵型中预留的间隙。

sentences.en: The Roman lines are subdivided into units called maniples.
sentences.zh: 罗马阵线被细分为被称为“中队”（maniples）的单位。

sentences.en: And if people think of maybe a checkerboard or on a die, a five, just lots and lots of those kind of fives that you get on dice all in a row.
sentences.zh: 如果人们想象一下国际象棋盘，或者骰子上的五点，就是骰子上那种一排排的五点。

sentences.en: You have a maniple, then you have a gap equivalent in length to the length of a maniple.
sentences.zh: 你有一个中队，然后是一个长度相当于一个中队的空隙。

sentences.en: Then you have another maniple and then you have another row behind it.
sentences.zh: 接着是另一个中队，然后它后面还有一排。

sentences.en: But the maniple is behind it is filling in the gap.
sentences.zh: 但后面的中队正好填补了前方的空隙。

sentences.en: But essentially, it means that you can constantly thread people through the gaps and move people up to fill gaps.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，这意味着你可以不断地让人员穿过间隙，并向前移动以填补空缺。

sentences.en: Can I?
sentences.zh: 我可以吗？

sentences.en: The depth of the maniples, it's on a stupefying scale.
sentences.zh: 中队的纵深达到了惊人的规模。

sentences.en: So it's perhaps five or six men across.
sentences.zh: 所以它的正面可能只有五到六个人宽。

sentences.en: And then you think if you're standing in that line, then next to you, there's a gap that's equivalent to five or six men.
sentences.zh: 然后你想想，如果你站在那个队列里，你旁边就是一个相当于五六个人宽的间隙。

sentences.en: And then another five or six men and then another gap and then another five or six men and then another gap.
sentences.zh: 然后又是五六个人，然后又是一个间隙，接着又是五六个人，再然后又是一个间隙。

sentences.en: And then standing behind you, you have maybe, it's maybe 30 deep.
sentences.zh: 而站在你身后的，可能有大约30排之深。

sentences.en: So when you put all the maniples together, the battle line is maybe 70 ranks deep.
sentences.zh: 所以当你把所有中队组合在一起时，战线可能有70排纵深。

sentences.en: So completely terrifying for the enemy.
sentences.zh: 这对敌人来说完全是极其恐怖的。

sentences.en: I mean, to be up against the line a mile and a half long that is that deep.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，面对一条有一英里半长、纵深如此之大的战线。

sentences.en: But there's also an additional advantage from the Roman point of view, which is bear in mind how raw many of the Roman recruits are.
sentences.zh: 但从罗马的角度来看，还有一个额外的优势，那就是想想许多罗马新兵是多么缺乏经验。

sentences.en: If you have lines that are that deep and you put your best, most seasoned men in the front and the others at the rear, it's very difficult for raw,
sentences.zh: 如果你有这么深的阵列，并且把你最优秀、最有经验的人放在前面，其他人放在后面，那么对于那些想要逃跑的新兵来说，

sentences.en: nervous recruits who might want to run away to do that because you're surrounded by people.
sentences.zh: 由于周围全都是人，他们很难做到这一点。

sentences.en: There's no way you can escape.
sentences.zh: 你根本无路可逃。

sentences.en: And so essentially, it's a way of kind of getting over the fact that perhaps these aren't the best trained troops that you could possibly have.
sentences.zh: 所以从本质上讲，这是一种克服这样一个事实的方法，即这些可能并不是你能找到的训练最好的军队。

sentences.en: So from your description, it sounds like an extremely meticulously devised, well-ordered, formidable military machine.
sentences.zh: 所以从你的描述听起来，这是一个极其精心设计、井然有序且令人生畏的军事机器。

sentences.en: But is there an argument that the sheer size and complexity of this system means that it's, frankly,
sentences.zh: 但有没有一种观点认为，这个系统庞大的规模和复杂性意味着，坦白说，

sentences.en: a bit lumbering and a bit overcomplicated and that Hannibal can actually exploit this?
sentences.zh: 它有点笨拙且过于复杂，以至于汉尼拔实际上可以利用这一点？

sentences.en: I think that you have seized on the weakness that Hannibal seizes on, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 我认为你抓住了汉尼拔所利用的弱点，多米尼克。

sentences.en: We're very similar people, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，我们俩真的很像。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly the problem with it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是它的问题所在。

sentences.en: The kind of the manipular system, which normally enables a Roman battle line to be very flexible.
sentences.zh: 那种通常能使罗马战线具有极高灵活性的中队系统。

sentences.en: These maniples are so deep that actually it's quite difficult and that there's a risk of them crunching up against one another,
sentences.zh: 这些中队纵深太大了，以至于实际上相当困难，并且它们彼此之间存在着挤压碰撞的风险。

sentences.en: in which case the flexibility would be completely loSt.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，灵活性就会荡然无存。

sentences.en: And I think Hannibal's aim is to try and apply pressure where it will force the sheer numbers of the Roman legions to come crunching into one another.
sentences.zh: 我认为汉尼拔的目标，是施加压力，迫使庞大的罗马军团密集地撞击在一起。

sentences.en: And in which case, its size, rather than being an advantage, then becomes a source of weakness.
sentences.zh: 如果是那样的话，它的规模非但不是优势，反而会成为劣势的根源。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it's a hugely difficult thing to pull off.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对是一件极其难以办到的事。

sentences.en: So the Roman plan, basically, is just to kind of advance and steamroll of the enemy.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马人的计划基本上就是推进并像蒸汽压路机一样碾压敌人。

sentences.en: Hannibal's dispositions are much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔的排兵布阵要复杂得多。

sentences.en: As usual, like the Romans have done, he stations his infantry in the center and his cavalry on the wings.
sentences.zh: 像罗马人惯常做的那样，他将步兵部署在中央，骑兵部署在两翼。

sentences.en: He has Mahabal, who's in command of the Numidian light cavalry, on the right wing.
sentences.zh: 他把马哈巴尔安排在右翼，由他指挥努米底亚轻骑兵。

sentences.en: So he is facing the allied cavalry commanded by Varro.
sentences.zh: 所以他面对的是由瓦罗指挥的同盟国骑兵。

sentences.en: On the left wing, so facing Paulus and the Roman cavalry, he's put the Spanish and Gallic heavy cavalry under the command of another very seasoned officer called, inevitably,
sentences.zh: 在左翼，也就是面对保卢斯和罗马骑兵的地方，他把西班牙和高卢重骑兵交由另一位经验极其丰富的军官指挥，这位军官毫无疑问就是——

sentences.en: Hasdrubal.
sentences.zh: 哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: So this isn't Hasdrubal the handsome.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是那个美男子哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: It's not Hasdrubal, who's Hannibal's brother.
sentences.zh: 也不是那个身为汉尼拔兄弟的哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: It's another Hasdrubal.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: I just assume they're all called Hasdrubal, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我甚至觉得他们全都叫哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: Yeah, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 对，差不多是这样。

sentences.en: Cavalry under Paulus, about three to one.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯麾下的骑兵，大约是三比一。

sentences.en: So that is where the Carthaginians have the advantage.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是迦太基人占优势的地方。

sentences.en: But obviously, when it comes to infantry, that is a very different story because the Carthaginians there are massively outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 但显然，说到步兵，情况就完全不同了，因为那里的迦太基人在数量上处于绝对劣势。

sentences.en: However, fortunately for Hannibal, he has a plan.
sentences.zh: 不过，幸亏汉尼拔早有计划。

sentences.en: And it's a very cunning plan.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个非常狡猾的计划。

sentences.en: So what he does is he draws up his Spanish and Gallic heavy infantry in a continuous line facing the Romans.
sentences.zh: 所以他是这样做的：他将西班牙和高卢重步兵排成一条面向罗马人的连续战线。

sentences.en: So stretching for almost a mile and a half.
sentences.zh: 绵延将近一点五英里长。

sentences.en: And compared to the Romans, this Carthaginian battle line is very, very slender.
sentences.zh: 与罗马人相比，这条迦太基战线显得非常非常单薄。

sentences.en: Hannibal stations himself and Mago, his younger brother, in the center of the line.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔和他的小弟马戈把自己部署在战线中央。

sentences.en: And he then leads the center of the line outwards towards the Roman lines.
sentences.zh: 然后他率领战线中央朝着罗马人的阵线凸出去。

sentences.en: So the effect is to create a kind of crescent.
sentences.zh: 所以这样做的效果是形成了一种新月形。

sentences.en: You know, the line starts to bulge outwards towards the Roman center.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，战线开始朝罗马人的中央凸起。

sentences.en: Hannibal's aim in doing this is to ensure that the Roman effort will be kind of focused on the middle of the plain.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔这样做的目的，是确保罗马人的进攻主要集中在平原中央。

sentences.en: And the reason that he does this is because he knows that this is how the legions fight.
sentences.zh: 他这么做的原因，是因为他深知军团就是这样战斗的。

sentences.en: That their aim is always to push through the middle of their enemy's battle line.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标永远是冲破敌人战线的中央。

sentences.en: If they do that, then they will inevitably break through the Carthaginian line because it's so thin relative to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 如果他们做到了这一点，就必然会突破迦太基人的战线，因为相对罗马人而言，这条战线实在太薄了。

sentences.en: At the Trebia, the Romans had done that.
sentences.zh: 在特雷比亚，罗马人就是这么干的。

sentences.en: And Hannibal hadn't been able to stop them then from kind of marching off and doing what they wanted.
sentences.zh: 当时汉尼拔没能阻止他们扬长而去、按自己的意愿行事。

sentences.en: But this time at Cannae, he has planned for this eventuality.
sentences.zh: 但这一次在坎尼，他已经为这种可能性做好了打算。

sentences.en: So he is assuming that in the long run, the Roman line will break through the Spaniards and the Gauls.
sentences.zh: 所以他预料从长远来看，罗马人的战线将会突破西班牙人和高卢人的防线。

sentences.en: And he has kept back the Libyans, who are like a kind of phalanx, great long spears, and equipped with Roman arms and Roman armor.
sentences.zh: 而他留下了利比亚人，他们就像某种方阵，手持长矛，装备着罗马武器和罗马盔甲。

sentences.en: So they actually look quite like the legionaries.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上看起来很像罗马军团士兵。

sentences.en: And these are Hannibal's best, most disciplined troops.
sentences.zh: 这些是汉尼拔手下最好、纪律性最强的部队。

sentences.en: And he has stationed them behind the front line and at an angle to it.
sentences.zh: 他把他们部署在最前线的后方，并与前线保持一定角度。

sentences.en: So that if you imagine the Romans break through the line of the Spaniards and Gauls, the Libyans are like a pair of pincers ready to close in.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，你可以想象，如果罗马人突破了西班牙人和高卢人的防线，利比亚人就像一把准备合拢的大钳子。

sentences.en: So the Romans will think that they've broken through.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马人会以为自己已经突破了防线。

sentences.en: They go rushing forwards.
sentences.zh: 他们会向前冲去。

sentences.en: The Libyans will close in and capture them on their flanks.
sentences.zh: 而利比亚人则会合围并从两翼包抄他们。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a difficult maneuver to pull off.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个很难执行的战术动作。

sentences.en: But obviously, if it does work, then potentially it's going to be very, very devastating in its effect.
sentences.zh: 但显然，如果它真的成功了，那么它的破坏效果将是极其巨大的。

sentences.en: So just to try and get our heads around this, what effectively he's doing, he's not exactly sacrificing his front line, but he's assuming that his front line will break.
sentences.zh: 所以为了让我们更好地理解这一点，他实际上在做的，倒不是确切地牺牲他的前线，而是假设他的前线会被击溃。

sentences.en: The Romans will break through.
sentences.zh: 罗马人会突破进来。

sentences.en: And his whole plan is that the Romans will break through.
sentences.zh: 他的整个计划就是让罗马人突破进来。

sentences.en: And then he's got these Libyans behind who will pour into the Roman flanks.
sentences.zh: 然后他身后还有这些利比亚人，会如潮水般涌向罗马人的两翼。

sentences.en: Like the jaws of a mouth with sharp teeth.
sentences.zh: 就像一张长着利齿的血盆大口。

sentences.en: The downside is you don't want to be the people in the front line.
sentences.zh: 缺点就是你绝对不想成为身处前线的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because he's basically decided you're expendable.
sentences.zh: 因为他基本上已经决定你们是可牺牲的了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but Hannibal has placed himself there.
sentences.zh: 对，但汉尼拔自己就站在那里。

sentences.en: But he's assuming that he will be, what, the Romans will just rush past him or that he will fall back?
sentences.zh: 但他以为自己会怎样呢？是罗马人直接冲过他身旁，还是他会撤退？

sentences.en: He's, again, backing himself, which is what he always does, that he will be able to inspire the men who are very, very loyal to him in the front row to fight as hard as possible.
sentences.zh: 他依然在押注自己——这也是他一贯的做法——坚信自己能够激励前排那些对他极为忠诚的士兵去进行最顽强的抵抗。

sentences.en: But it's accepted that at some point it will break.
sentences.zh: 但大家都接受了防线在某个时刻会被突破的现实。

sentences.en: And then he has to hope that the Libyans will be able to play the role that he's assigned them.
sentences.zh: 然后他就只能寄希望于利比亚人能够扮演好他所指定的角色。

sentences.en: It's a dangerous, complicated plan, but it is a plan.
sentences.zh: 这是一个危险且复杂的计划，但它确实是个计划。

sentences.en: And, of course, the other factor is that if the Libyans are able to seal the broken line in the front, you also have the cavalry in the rear who can then come up.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一个因素是，如果利比亚人能够封堵住前线被击溃的缺口，你身后还有骑兵可以随之杀到。

sentences.en: If they've swept away the Roman and Italian cavalry, they can then come galloping around and crash into the rear of the Roman army.
sentences.zh: 如果他们已经横扫了罗马和意大利骑兵，他们就可以从旁迂回，雷霆万钧般撞击罗马军队的后方。

sentences.en: And then you will have the whole army surrounded.
sentences.zh: 到了那时，整支军队都会被包围。

sentences.en: And this has always been kind of Hannibal's, you know, dream.
sentences.zh: 这一直以来可以说是汉尼拔的梦想。

sentences.en: This is what he wants.
sentences.zh: 这就是他梦寐以求的。

sentences.en: And he will have his battle of annihilation.
sentences.zh: 他将迎来属于他的歼灭战。

sentences.en: But as I say, it's a complicated plan.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，这是一个复杂的计划。

sentences.en: So let's see what happens and see how it works out.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们拭目以待，看看结果会如何。

sentences.en: So the battle lines are drawn up.
sentences.zh: 双方的战线就这样拉开了。

sentences.en: And I think there's always this sense of nervous anticipation before it happens.
sentences.zh: 我想在此之前总有一种紧张期待的心情。

sentences.en: There's lots of maneuvering.
sentences.zh: 有大量的排兵布阵。

sentences.en: There's kind of blasting of trumpets.
sentences.zh: 伴随着阵阵号角声。

sentences.en: And then you just wait.
sentences.zh: 然后你只需等待。

sentences.en: And you can imagine, you know, it's getting hotter.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，天气越来越热。

sentences.en: The sun is rising in the sky.
sentences.zh: 太阳在空中升起。

sentences.en: The shields are starting to feel heavier on the arm.
sentences.zh: 手臂上的盾牌开始变得越来越沉重。

sentences.en: Sweat around, you know, as you hold your spears or whatever.
sentences.zh: 握着长矛之类的武器时，四周满是汗水。

sentences.en: I mean, very, very nerve-wracking.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真是极其折磨神经。

sentences.en: Because it's nerve-wracking, ultimately, the time comes where people think, oh, hang this.
sentences.zh: 正因为备受煎熬，最终大家都会觉得，管他呢。

sentences.en: Let's get on with it.
sentences.zh: 大干一场吧。

sentences.en: And the people who begin are the skirmishers.
sentences.zh: 率先出击的是轻装兵。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians, again, are outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人再次在数量上处于劣势。

sentences.en: But they are much, much more proficient than the Velites, the Roman skirmishers in their wolf clothes and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但他们比那些穿着狼皮之类的罗马轻步兵要精锐得多。

sentences.en: And in particular, the Balearic slingers, my favorite, are absolutely lethal.
sentences.zh: 尤其是巴利阿里投石手，我最喜欢的兵种，绝对是致命的存在。

sentences.en: So they have a much longer range than the Velites do with their little spears.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的射程比那些拿着短矛的罗马轻步兵要远得多。

sentences.en: They're very accurate.
sentences.zh: 他们非常精准。

sentences.en: The slingshot is coming out.
sentences.zh: 投石索纷纷出击。

sentences.en: You know, you've got all this dust blowing up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，漫天尘土飞扬。

sentences.en: Very difficult to see the slingshot as it comes.
sentences.zh: 飞石袭来时极难看清。

sentences.en: If it hits you on the helm, it is possible to kind of knock you out.
sentences.zh: 如果它砸中你的头盔，完全有可能把你砸得失去知觉。

sentences.en: And so, understandably, the Roman infantry decide, well, we don't want this.
sentences.zh: 因此，可以理解的是，罗马步兵决定：好吧，我们可不想吃这个亏。

sentences.en: You know, get rid of the Velites.
sentences.zh: 把轻步兵撤下去吧。

sentences.en: The Velites withdraw.
sentences.zh: 轻步兵撤退了。

sentences.en: This is Daly's theory.
sentences.zh: 这就是戴利的理论。

sentences.en: I think he's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是对的。

sentences.en: They go right the way back behind the full line of the Roman heavy infantry.
sentences.zh: 他们一直退到了罗马重步兵完整阵线的正后方。

sentences.en: And this then means that the front line of the Roman heavy infantry are in a position to advance.
sentences.zh: 这意味着罗马重步兵的前线已经做好了推进的准备。

sentences.en: This is what's been going on in the opening maneuvers of the battle.
sentences.zh: 这就是战斗刚拉开帷幕时所发生的情况。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, you've got the cavalry.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，骑兵那边也在行动。

sentences.en: And on the banks of the Ophidius, the river, which is where Hasdrubal's Spanish and Gallic heavy cavalry are facing Paulus' Roman horse, it is all kicking off.
sentences.zh: 在奥菲迪乌斯河畔，哈斯德鲁巴的西班牙和高卢重骑兵正在那里面对保卢斯麾下的罗马骑兵，战局一触即发。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginians, even as the skirmishers are still doing their stuff with their javelins and their slingshot and stuff,
sentences.zh: 就在轻步兵们还在用标枪和投石索大显身手的时候，

sentences.en: the Carthaginian cavalry are herring towards the Romans.
sentences.zh: 迦太基骑兵已经朝着罗马人疾驰而去了。

sentences.en: They just pile into Paulus and his men.
sentences.zh: 他们直接猛扑向保卢斯和他的部下。

sentences.en: And there's a story in Plutarch that Paulus is wounded, that he has to dismount, that all his officers around him think, oh, well, he's doing it.
sentences.zh: 普鲁塔克记载了一个故事：保卢斯负伤了，不得不下马，他周围的所有军官都觉得，既然他都下马了，

sentences.en: We better do it.
sentences.zh: 我们也照办吧。

sentences.en: They dismount.
sentences.zh: 于是他们也下了马。

sentences.en: And then the whole Roman force dismounts.
sentences.zh: 接着，整个罗马军队都下了马。

sentences.en: And it may be that this is a kind of an attempt by the Romans to explain why it is that the Roman horse put up such a weak show.
sentences.zh: 这或许是罗马人试图解释为什么罗马骑兵表现得如此软弱的一种借口。

sentences.en: Anyway, they are absolutely swept away.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他们彻底被击溃了。

sentences.en: They have not managed to put up a fight at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没能组织起像样的抵抗。

sentences.en: Paulus is able to clamber his way into the main body of the infantry.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯设法挤回了步兵主力阵营中。

sentences.en: So he is able to survive this route.
sentences.zh: 所以他在这次溃败中幸存了下来。

sentences.en: But, I mean, it's very poor on the part of the Roman horse and brilliant for Hasdrubal and his men who have swept the Roman flank clear.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，罗马骑兵的表现实在太差劲了，而哈斯德鲁巴及其部下的表现则堪称辉煌，他们已经清空了罗马人的侧翼。

sentences.en: And Hasdrubal does not do a Prince Rupert.
sentences.zh: 而哈斯德鲁巴并没有效仿鲁珀特亲王。

sentences.en: So he doesn't go herring off after the Roman cavalry.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有尾随追击罗马骑兵盲目狂奔。

sentences.en: He wheels round and he looks at the state of battle and what he decides to do, we will come to in due course.
sentences.zh: 他调转马头观察战局，并决定下一步采取什么行动，我们稍后就会讲到。

sentences.en: Because, meanwhile, in the main field of battle, where the two great blocks of infantry are facing one another, clash point is happening.
sentences.zh: 因为与此同时，在两大步兵方阵对峙的主战场上，激战正酣。

sentences.en: So what's going on with the infantry?
sentences.zh: 步兵那边情况如何？

sentences.en: So the Roman young men, but probably the best, the most seasoned, the most proficient in fighting, have been stationed in the front rank.
sentences.zh: 罗马的年轻士兵们——很可能是其中最好、最老练、作战最精锐的部队——被部署在了最前排。

sentences.en: They are smashing their weapons on their wooden shields, you know, kind of terrifying counterpart to this great nodding crests that they have on their helmets.
sentences.zh: 他们用武器疯狂敲击着木质盾牌，与他们头盔上那些巨大的摇曳饰羽相呼应，显得格外骇人。

sentences.en: You know, their armor is brilliantly polished.
sentences.zh: 他们的盔甲被打磨得光彩夺目。

sentences.en: And on the other side, you have the Spaniards and the Gauls.
sentences.zh: 而在另一边，则是西班牙人和高卢人。

sentences.en: They are holding their position.
sentences.zh: 他们坚守着阵地。

sentences.en: Remember the front of the bulge, very, very close to the Roman line.
sentences.zh: 还记得那个凸起的弧形阵线前沿吗，距离罗马防线非常非常近。

sentences.en: They're raising their own war cries.
sentences.zh: 他们也在高呼自己的战呐。

sentences.en: The Gallic war cries in particular, notorious.
sentences.zh: 尤其是高卢人的战呐，向来声名狼藉。

sentences.en: They also have their, you know, these trumpets, the carnics, terrifying din.
sentences.zh: 他们还吹奏着那种名为卡尼克斯的长号，制造出恐怖的喧嚣。

sentences.en: And this is an age where people generally are not used to loud noise in the way that we are in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人们通常不习惯21世纪这种震耳欲聋噪音的时代。

sentences.en: So the din of the, you know, is overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 所以这种喧嚣声简直震耳欲聋。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so it's not surprising that the moment that the skirmishers are out of the way, the Romans charge.
sentences.zh: 因此，毫不意外的是，一旦轻步兵撤开，罗马人便发起了冲锋。

sentences.en: They're thinking, you know, let's get this over and done with.
sentences.zh: 他们心想：赶紧把这场仗打完吧。

sentences.en: The sooner this is done, the better for all concerned.
sentences.zh: 这事儿早点结束对所有人都有好处。

sentences.en: So the Hastati, they advance.
sentences.zh: 于是哈斯塔蒂步兵开始推进。

sentences.en: The front ranks, probably the front two or three, because, you know, they don't want to start hitting their own men with javelins.
sentences.zh: 最前排的士兵，大概是前两排或前三排——因为他们可不想用标枪误伤自己人，

sentences.en: They hurl them.
sentences.zh: 他们投出了标枪。

sentences.en: The effect of this is less effective than normal because effectively they, you know, because of the bulge of the Carthaginian line,
sentences.zh: 由于迦太基战线的凸起，这种攻击的效果比平时要差一些，因为实际上，

sentences.en: they can't actually reach most of the Carthaginian front line with their spears.
sentences.zh: 他们的长矛根本够不到大多数迦太基前线士兵。

sentences.en: And then they charge and the hope is that they will be able to break the enemy so that they just go running away and then the killing can start.
sentences.zh: 接着他们发起冲锋，本希望能够击溃敌人，让敌人落荒而逃，然后就可以开始杀戮了。

sentences.en: But this doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有发生。

sentences.en: The Spaniards and Gauls hold their positions, partly because they're very seasoned veterans by this point, partly because Hannibal and Mago is there with them in the front rank,
sentences.zh: 西班牙人和高卢人坚守阵地，部分原因在于他们此时已是经验丰富的老兵，部分原因在于汉尼拔和马戈与他们并肩站在前排，

sentences.en: and partly because they just hate the Romans.
sentences.zh: 还部分原因在于他们对罗马人恨之入骨。

sentences.en: And probably they trust in Hannibal that his strategy is going to work and that they're going to have their vengeance.
sentences.zh: 他们可能也坚信汉尼拔的战略一定会奏效，他们将报仇雪恨。

sentences.en: They understand also how important a role that they have, how important it is that they maintain their position for as long as they possibly can.
sentences.zh: 他们同样明白自己肩负的角色有多么重要，尽可能持久地坚守阵地是多么关键。

sentences.en: And Daly in his book explains why.
sentences.zh: 戴利在他的书中解释了原因所在。

sentences.en: It was absolutely necessary for the peculiar crescent formation to be maintained so that the thin horns of the crescent, so that's the two flanks,
sentences.zh: 为了维持那种奇特的新月形阵型，绝对必须让新月那单薄的尖角——也就是两个侧翼，

sentences.en: would be kept out of the fighting for as long as possible.
sentences.zh: 尽可能长时间地远离战斗。

sentences.en: Because if the troops there broke early in the battle, the entire Carthaginian plan would collapse.
sentences.zh: 因为如果那里的部队在战斗初期崩溃，整个迦太基人的计划就会彻底瓦解。

sentences.en: So in other words,
sentences.zh: 换句话说就是

sentences.en: it's vital for Hannibal that the Roman forces are funneled into the center so that they can go into the kind of the mouth of these two Libyan jaws that are waiting to snap shut on them.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔至关重要的是，罗马军队被引导到中心，这样他们就能进入两支利比亚之钳的口中，等待着向他们猛然合拢。

sentences.en: It's a very kind of grinding clash.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常残酷的绞杀战。

sentences.en: It's kind of man on man.
sentences.zh: 这有点像人与人的近身搏斗。

sentences.en: And effectively, the whole line is this kind of series of duels between Gauls and Spaniards against Romans.
sentences.zh: 实际上，整个战线就是高卢人和西班牙人与罗马人之间的一系列决斗。

sentences.en: The Romans and the Spaniards are both armed with stabbing swords.
sentences.zh: 罗马人和西班牙人都配备了刺剑。

sentences.en: So they're both aiming that, you know, they're aiming at the abdomen.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的目标都是，你知道的，他们把目标对准了腹部。

sentences.en: The Gauls have slashing swords.
sentences.zh: 高卢人使用的是砍剑。

sentences.en: So they're aiming at the shoulders.
sentences.zh: 所以他们瞄准的是肩膀。

sentences.en: And most of the wounds, because both sides have shields, are probably to parts of the body that aren't protected by either the shield or by armour.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数伤口，因为双方都有盾牌，可能都出现在既没有盾牌也没有盔甲保护的身体部位。

sentences.en: So that's heads, legs, sword arMs.
sentences.zh: 所以那是头部、腿部、挥剑的手臂。

sentences.en: If you get too many wounds on your leg or your arm or to your head, then obviously you start to weaken.
sentences.zh: 如果你的腿、手臂或头部受了太多伤，那么很明显你就会开始虚弱。

sentences.en: You might lose your balance, your ability to continue fighting.
sentences.zh: 你可能会失去平衡，失去继续战斗的能力。

sentences.en: You might fall to the ground.
sentences.zh: 你可能会摔倒在地上。

sentences.en: And the moment you fall to the ground, that's it.
sentences.zh: 而你一旦摔倒在地上，那就完了。

sentences.en: You're dead.
sentences.zh: 你死定了。

sentences.en: You know, you're going to be a blow to your head.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你的头部会受到重击。

sentences.en: Or just trampled underfoot.
sentences.zh: 或者直接被踩在脚下。

sentences.en: Trampled underfoot.
sentences.zh: 被踩在脚下。

sentences.en: And of course, the more bodies are trampled underfoot, the more they rise, the more slippery the ground becomes because blood is starting to spill out and, you know,
sentences.zh: 当然，被踩在脚下的尸体越多，它们堆积得越高，地面就变得越滑，因为鲜血开始流淌，而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: moisten the dust that is everywhere.
sentences.zh: 浸湿了无处不在的尘土。

sentences.en: And you have exhaustion as well because the sun is rising higher and higher in the sky.
sentences.zh: 而且你还要忍受精疲力竭，因为太阳在天空中越升越高。

sentences.en: You've got the dust blowing in.
sentences.zh: 风把尘土吹得漫天飞舞。

sentences.en: And the estimate is that men can't really fight in this way for more than 15 minutes at a stretch.
sentences.zh: 据估计，士兵们这样连续战斗的时间实际上不会超过15分钟。

sentences.en: So the lines, you want to think of it, the lines are kind of engaging, then withdrawing, engaging, then withdrawing.
sentences.zh: 所以战线，你可以这样想象，战线先是交锋，然后撤退，再交锋，再撤退。

sentences.en: Kind of almost the rhythm of a really brutal sporting encounter, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，这几乎就像是一场极其残酷的体育比赛的节奏。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, very intense moments of engagement and then the players withdraw and kind of draw their breath and then back in again.
sentences.zh: 你知道，非常激烈的交锋时刻，然后队员们撤退，喘口气，接着又冲上去。

sentences.en: And just physically relentless and demanding.
sentences.zh: 而且在体力上极其残酷和严苛。

sentences.en: But the advantage of the Roman manipular system is that people, you know, men who just become too tired or too wounded can be withdrawn and they can funnel more people forward.
sentences.zh: 但罗马军团制的好处在于，人们，你知道的，那些变得太累或受伤太重的士兵可以撤下来，他们可以把更多的人输送到前方。

sentences.en: So there is this kind of relentless sense of fresh men coming to the front line.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一种源源不断的新生力量赶到前线的紧迫感。

sentences.en: And so it's unsurprising that as the fighting goes on, although the Gauls and Spaniards fight with the utmost ferocity and implacability,
sentences.zh: 所以毫不奇怪，随着战斗的继续，尽管高卢人和西班牙人以极其凶猛和冷酷的态度战斗，

sentences.en: the Roman weight of numbers does start to tell.
sentences.zh: 罗马人庞大的兵力优势开始显现出来了。

sentences.en: And as the Roman front line grinds forward, the crescent that the Gauls and the Spaniards have formed starts to flatten and then to buckle and to be pushed backwards.
sentences.zh: 随着罗马前线向前推进，高卢人和西班牙人形成的月牙形开始变平，接着弯曲并被向后推去。

sentences.en: And the Romans in the centre give a great cheer.
sentences.zh: 正中央的罗马人发出了一声巨大的欢呼。

sentences.en: They consent victory.
sentences.zh: 他们认为胜利在望。

sentences.en: They push forwards.
sentences.zh: 他们向前冲去。

sentences.en: Space opens up behind them as they do so.
sentences.zh: 当他们这样做时，他们身后露出了空间。

sentences.en: More troops come filling in to fill the gap.
sentences.zh: 更多的军队涌来填补空隙。

sentences.en: The order of the maniples starts to be loSt.
sentences.zh: 军团的阵型开始变得混乱。

sentences.en: It's a great, excited crush because everyone wants to share in the victory.
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨大而狂热的拥挤，因为每个人都想分享胜利。

sentences.en: Cries of joy, of triumph kind of rippling through the entire Roman battle line.
sentences.zh: 喜悦和凯旋的欢呼声在整个罗马战线上回荡。

sentences.en: The feeling is absolutely that the battle is won.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉绝对是这场战役已经赢了。

sentences.en: But of course, Hannibal still has his two deadly cards to play.
sentences.zh: 但当然，汉尼拔手中还有两张致命的牌要打。

sentences.en: And as the Gauls and Spaniards retreat, space has opened up for the Libyans who are hitherto being held in reserve to crash into the flanks of the advancing Romans.
sentences.zh: 随着高卢人和西班牙人的撤退，一直被作为预备队保留的利比亚人有了空间，他们猛烈撞击着正在前进的罗马人的侧翼。

sentences.en: And it happens exactly as Hannibal has planned.
sentences.zh: 一切都正如汉尼拔所计划的那样发生了。

sentences.en: I mean, it couldn't go better because by now the Romans are so tightly packed that they haven't got any opportunity to manoeuvre.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不可能比这更好了，因为到目前为止罗马人挤得太紧了，他们根本没有机会进行战术机动。

sentences.en: And in fact, it's quite difficult for them even to kind of, you know, raise their sword arMs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们甚至很难，你知道的，连举起挥剑的手臂都很困难。

sentences.en: And you just have this kind of great scrum of men who are being slowly crushed together by the Libyan phalanxes to their left and to their right.
sentences.zh: 你会看到一大群人被左侧和右侧的利比亚方阵慢慢挤压在一起。

sentences.en: And ahead of them, the Gauls and the Spaniards who had been retreating, you know, they get a second wind.
sentences.zh: 而在他们前方，一直在撤退的高卢人和西班牙人，你知道的，他们恢复了体力。

sentences.en: They sense that the balance of the battle has changed.
sentences.zh: 他们感觉到战局的天平已经倾斜。

sentences.en: They turn around.
sentences.zh: 他们转过身来。

sentences.en: They block the Roman advance.
sentences.zh: 他们挡住了罗马人的推进。

sentences.en: And the absolute horror for the Romans is that one minute they think they're winning.
sentences.zh: 对罗马人来说，绝对的恐怖在于，前一刻他们还以为自己赢了。

sentences.en: The battle is won.
sentences.zh: 这场战斗已经赢了。

sentences.en: And then suddenly they find themselves surrounded on three sides by people who are not fleeing at all.
sentences.zh: 然后突然发现自己三面都被那些根本没有逃跑的人包围了。

sentences.en: And the Libyans are completely fresh.
sentences.zh: 而且利比亚人精力完全充沛。

sentences.en: And more than that, they actually look like Romans.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们看起来甚至很像罗马人。

sentences.en: So it must have come as a massive surprise for the Romans to suddenly find them crashing into them.
sentences.zh: 因此，当敌人突然向他们发起猛烈攻击时，罗马人一定感到了极大的震惊。

sentences.en: So a horrible situation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可怕的处境。

sentences.en: And the Romans didn't anticipate this at all.
sentences.zh: 而罗马人对此毫无预料。

sentences.en: I mean, you would think that practiced commanders would see the crescent shape and they would think,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你本以为经验丰富的指挥官会看到月牙形的阵型，他们会想，

sentences.en: well, the one thing we don't want to happen is for our boys to be enveloped by the flanks of this crescent.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们最不希望发生的事情就是我们的士兵被这个月牙形的两翼包围。

sentences.en: And yet they've walked straight into it.
sentences.zh: 然而他们却径直走进了这个陷阱。

sentences.en: Because they're trusting their weight of numbers, because that's how they fight, because they're not geniuses like Hannibal, because the men that they have are not seasoned.
sentences.zh: 因为他们盲目相信庞大的兵力，因为他们一向如此战斗，因为他们不是汉尼拔这样的天才，因为他们手下的士兵缺乏历练。

sentences.en: They can't kind of think on their feet.
sentences.zh: 他们不能随机应变。

sentences.en: They're not practiced at maneuvering.
sentences.zh: 他们不习惯灵活调度。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is the mark of Hannibal's genius is that he, you know, he's exploiting all of that.
sentences.zh: 当然，这正是汉尼拔天才的标志，他，你知道的，他正在利用这一切。

sentences.en: And he's like a judo thrower, turning his enemy's strength into a weakness.
sentences.zh: 他就像一个柔道高手，将敌人的力量转化为弱点。

sentences.en: And you said he had two cards to play.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说他还有两张王牌要打。

sentences.en: He's played one, which was the Libyans.
sentences.zh: 他已经打出了一张，那就是利比亚人。

sentences.en: Now, the second, of course, you mentioned it before, Hasdrubal and the heavy cavalry.
sentences.zh: 现在，第二张，当然，你之前提到过，是哈斯德鲁巴和重骑兵。

sentences.en: As you said, they haven't gone shooting off.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们并没有盲目冲出去。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: They now return to the fray, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们现在重新加入了战斗，不是吗？

sentences.en: People may remember that they've swept away Paulus, who has gone to join the main body of the infantry.
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得，他们已经消灭了保卢斯，后者已经去加入了步兵主力。

sentences.en: The rest of the Roman cavalry have been swept away from the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 其余的罗马骑兵已经被赶出了战场。

sentences.en: So what Hasdrubal does is he then turns around the length of the Roman infantry to go to the other wing,
sentences.zh: 因此，哈斯德鲁巴所做的是，他沿着罗马步兵的阵线迂回过去，前往另一个侧翼，

sentences.en: where the Numidians under Mahabal have been having a standoff with the Italians under Varro, because the Numidians are light.
sentences.zh: 马哈巴尔率领的努米底亚人正在那里与瓦罗率领的意大利人对峙，因为努米底亚人是轻骑兵。

sentences.en: They don't want to engage with the Italian cavalry.
sentences.zh: 他们不想与意大利骑兵正面交锋。

sentences.en: But now suddenly Hasdrubal and his heavy cavalry come sweeping up.
sentences.zh: 但现在哈斯德鲁巴和他的重骑兵突然席卷而至。

sentences.en: The Italians are swept away again.
sentences.zh: 意大利人再次被击溃。

sentences.en: Varro is swept away with them.
sentences.zh: 瓦罗也随之溃败。

sentences.en: So he's gone from the scene of the battle.
sentences.zh: 所以他已经退出了战场。

sentences.en: Well, he survives, but he's now gone.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他活了下来，但他现在已经不在了。

sentences.en: This means that Hasdrubal and his heavy cavalry can now crash into the rear of the Roman infantry.
sentences.zh: 这意味着哈斯德鲁巴和他的重骑兵现在可以猛烈冲向罗马步兵的后方。

sentences.en: And the likelihood is the infantry in the rear of the Roman battle line are not the seasoned veterans with their long spears who could have formed a phalanx and kept the cavalry away,
sentences.zh: 极有可能的是，处于罗马战线后方的步兵并不是那些拥有长矛、能够组成方阵并将骑兵挡在身外的百战老兵，

sentences.en: but the velites, the skirmishers with their wolfskins.
sentences.zh: 而是身披狼皮的轻步兵、散兵。

sentences.en: And there is nothing that they can do against heavy cavalry.
sentences.zh: 面对重骑兵，他们无能为力。

sentences.en: So in that description by Livy, you read of the battlefield the day after the battle, there was an account of men lying there whose tendons had been sliced and who can't move.
sentences.zh: 因此，在你阅读李维对战后第二天战场的描述时，有这样一则记录：地上躺着一些脚腱被割断、无法动弹的人。

sentences.en: And this, I think, is what Hasdrubal's cavalry are doing.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是哈斯德鲁巴的骑兵所做的事情。

sentences.en: As they gallop in, if they can't kill someone, they just slice the tendons and leave them there to exsanguinate, to the blood to spill out.
sentences.zh: 当他们呼啸冲入时，如果无法杀死某人，他们就会割断对方的脚腱，将其留在那里流血过多而死。

sentences.en: And then they start crashing forwards.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始向前猛冲。

sentences.en: And the press of Romans trying to withdraw pushes back in.
sentences.zh: 试图撤退的罗马人相互推挤着退了回去。

sentences.en: And the whole Roman army now is surrounded.
sentences.zh: 现在整个罗马军队都被包围了。

sentences.en: You've got the Gauls and the Spaniards on the front.
sentences.zh: 正面是高卢人和西班牙人。

sentences.en: You've got the Libyans on the flanks.
sentences.zh: 两翼是利比亚人。

sentences.en: You've got Hasdrubal's cavalry in the rear.
sentences.zh: 后方是哈斯德鲁巴的骑兵。

sentences.en: The process of annihilation is now set in train and it takes Hannibal's men many hours.
sentences.zh: 歼灭过程现在已经开始，汉尼拔的士兵花费了许多个小时。

sentences.en: And it must have been a hideous experience for everyone.
sentences.zh: 对每个人来说，这一定是一次可怕的经历。

sentences.en: I mean, completely exhausting, even for Hannibal's men.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使对汉尼拔的士兵来说，也完全精疲力竭。

sentences.en: You know, their shields are heavy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们的盾牌很重。

sentences.en: Their sword arms are starting to ache.
sentences.zh: 他们挥剑的手臂开始酸痛。

sentences.en: They're drenched in sweat.
sentences.zh: 他们大汗淋漓。

sentences.en: Lots of them are wounded.
sentences.zh: 他们当中很多人都受伤了。

sentences.en: And I imagine that as the battle goes on, so the kind of the pauses between the bouts of combat go longer and longer.
sentences.zh: 我能想象，随着战斗的进行，两场激战之间的间歇变得越来越长。

sentences.en: And for the Romans trapped inside, I mean, this just must have been.
sentences.zh: 对于被困在里面的罗马人来说，我的意思是，这简直是……

sentences.en: And we're talking about tens of thousands of men.
sentences.zh: 而且我们讨论的是成千上万的人。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人。

sentences.en: So some of them manage to escape.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些人设法逃脱了。

sentences.en: You know, there are kind of gaps in the Carthaginian line they can get out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，迦太基防线有一些缺口他们可以逃出去。

sentences.en: Some of the Italian allies surrender and that's fine.
sentences.zh: 一些意大利盟友投降了，这没关系。

sentences.en: You know, Hannibal's policy is absolutely to accept their surrender.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，汉尼拔的政策绝对是接受他们的投降。

sentences.en: But the Romans, though, you know, most of them stand their ground.
sentences.zh: 不过罗马人，你知道的，他们大多数人坚守阵地。

sentences.en: A refusal to submit is the essence of what being a Roman is.
sentences.zh: 拒绝屈服是身为罗马人的核心本质。

sentences.en: It's the quality that's most admired in the Republic.
sentences.zh: 这是共和国最受赞赏的品质。

sentences.en: And I think it's hard to overemphasize the horror of their fate, the physical crush, the panic and the certainty of approaching death.
sentences.zh: 我认为怎么强调他们命运的可怕、肉体的挤压、恐慌以及对即将来临的死亡的确定感都不为过。

sentences.en: Because if you're in the center of this kind of great crush of men, imagine, you know, you don't really know what's happening.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你处于这种巨大的人群挤压中心，想象一下，你知道的，你并不知道到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And then the news comes to you about what's happened.
sentences.zh: 然后有关发生了什么的消息传到了你这里。

sentences.en: You're stuck there waiting for the Carthaginian swords and spears to reach you.
sentences.zh: 你被困在那里，等待着迦太基人的刀剑和长矛向你刺来。

sentences.en: I mean, just hideous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，简直太可怕了。

sentences.en: People start to void their bowels, to urinate with terror, to vomit.
sentences.zh: 人们开始大小便失禁，因惊恐而小便，甚至呕吐。

sentences.en: Piles of corpses are starting to rise.
sentences.zh: 尸体堆开始越积越高。

sentences.en: The sun is high in the sky, so they're starting to smell.
sentences.zh: 太阳高悬在天空中，所以尸体开始发臭。

sentences.en: It's drifting across the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 恶臭在战场上弥漫开来。

sentences.en: Death from the air.
sentences.zh: 来自空中的死亡。

sentences.en: Slingshot is starting to rain down again.
sentences.zh: 投石索的弹丸又开始如雨点般落下。

sentences.en: You've still got this blinding dust and blood just everywhere, drenching it.
sentences.zh: 你依然置身于无处不在的刺眼尘土和浸透一切的鲜血之中。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like wading through a sea of blood and viscera.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像是在血海和内脏中蹚行。

sentences.en: And I think the trauma of it is most grotesquely and unsettlingly illustrated in that passage that you opened this episode with.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你在本集开篇所引用的那段文字中，对这种创伤的描绘最为诡异也最令人不安。

sentences.en: People may remember that Livy reports how the day after the Carthaginians inspect the battlefield and they find among the Roman dead some with their heads buried in the ground.
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得，李维报道说，战后第二天，迦太基人视察战场，发现有些罗马死者的头部埋在土里。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't believe that's true.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不敢相信这是真的。

sentences.en: But if it is, then it's either kind of suicide or an attempt to hide from the horrors of the battle.
sentences.zh: 但如果是真的，那要么是一种自杀行为，要么是试图躲避战争的恐怖。

sentences.en: And the fact that Livy records it, I mean, it must have been a story that was current at the time and therefore surely reflective of the scale of the horror.
sentences.zh: 鉴于李维将其记录下来，我的意思是，这在当时一定是个广为流传的故事，因此无疑反映了恐怖的程度。

sentences.en: And by the end of the day, upwards of, you know, I mean, tens of thousands of Romans are dead.
sentences.zh: 到了一天结束时，你知道的，有高达数万名罗马人丧生。

sentences.en: Yeah, just looking at the estimates, between 50 and 70,000 men probably were killed.
sentences.zh: 是的，看看估计数字，可能有5到7万人被杀。

sentences.en: I mean, just absolutely massacred where they stood.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，简直就是在他们站立的地方被大肆屠杀。

sentences.en: And, you know, for Hannibal, this must be a victory beyond his wildest dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，对汉尼拔来说，这一定是一场超越他最大胆想象的胜利。

sentences.en: I mean, just a staggering success, a vindication of his tactics, of his approach.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一次令人震惊的巨大成功，是对他战术和方法的证明。

sentences.en: He has absolutely annihilated this Roman army and brought the Romans to their lowest ebb.
sentences.zh: 他彻底消灭了这支罗马军队，把罗马人逼到了最低谷。

sentences.en: I mean, I think you could say it's the most astonishing, the most remarkable victory that any general had ever won in history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为你可以说这是历史上任何将领赢得的最惊人、最卓越的胜利。

sentences.en: And that is why it continues to be studied and admired by military strategists to this day.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么直到今天它仍然受到军事战略家的研究和赞誉。

sentences.en: And you can't say that of any other ancient battle.
sentences.zh: 你不能对任何其他古代战役这样说。

sentences.en: It has a kind of perfection, a terrifying perfection about it.
sentences.zh: 它有一种完美，一种可怕的完美。

sentences.en: And yet he hasn't won the war.
sentences.zh: 然而他并没有赢得这场战争。

sentences.en: Because the question now is, what will the Romans do?
sentences.zh: 因为现在的问题是，罗马人会怎么做？

sentences.en: Will they sue for peace?
sentences.zh: 他们会求和吗？

sentences.en: You know, where does he go from here?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他接下来要去哪里？

sentences.en: Does he march on Rome?
sentences.zh: 他会进军罗马吗？

sentences.en: Does he try to destroy the Republic?
sentences.zh: 他会试图摧毁共和国吗？

sentences.en: Or have the Romans got one more comeback left in them, Tom?
sentences.zh: 还是说罗马人手里还留着最后一次反击的机会，汤姆？

sentences.en: Do you know, Dominic, we are going to leave that question as a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，多米尼克，我们要把这个问题留作一个悬念。

sentences.en: We are going to end our series on the rise of Hannibal at this point.
sentences.zh: 我们关于汉尼拔崛起的系列节目就在这里结束。

sentences.en: Hannibal has attained the absolute pinnacle of everything he could have dreamed of.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔已经达到了他梦寐以求的一切的绝对巅峰。

sentences.en: But as you say, there is still the fact that Rome is not yet defeated.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，罗马尚未被击败，这是一个不争的事实。

sentences.en: Should Hannibal march on Rome?
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔应该进军罗马吗？

sentences.en: What's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 将会发生什么？

sentences.en: And we will hopefully answer those questions with a third series, which will take the story forwards.
sentences.zh: 我们希望能在第三季中回答这些问题，将故事继续推进。

sentences.en: And that series as well will end on a terrible note.
sentences.zh: 而且那个系列也将以一个糟糕的结局收尾。

sentences.en: We love a terrible note on the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 我们《The Rest is History》最喜欢糟糕的结局了。

sentences.en: We also like to torment and tantalise our listeners by leaving them hanging at the end of the series.
sentences.zh: 我们也喜欢把听众吊在系列节目的结尾，以此来折磨和撩拨他们。

sentences.en: And that's what we've done.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所做的。

sentences.en: We've had season one.
sentences.zh: 我们有了第一季。

sentences.en: We've had season two.
sentences.zh: 我们有了第二季。

sentences.en: Season three will be coming.
sentences.zh: 第三季即将到来。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So next week, we will be back with something very different.
sentences.zh: 所以下周，我们将带着完全不同的内容回归。

sentences.en: We'll still be in Italy, but we will be in the golden age of Renaissance Florence for the story of the Medici.
sentences.zh: 我们仍将身处意大利，但我们将进入文艺复兴时期佛罗伦萨的黄金时代，讲述美第奇家族的故事。

sentences.en: But Tom, thank you so much for that.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，非常感谢你的精彩讲述。

sentences.en: The rest is history podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是《The Rest is History》播客。

sentences.en: Dust and blood.
sentences.zh: 尘土与鲜血。

sentences.en: Dust and blood.
sentences.zh: 尘土与鲜血。

sentences.en: We love it.
sentences.zh: 我们爱极了。

sentences.en: On that bombshell, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 伴随着这个重磅消息，非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: And goodbye, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。
